articles.title: BOJ's Tamura Says Half-Point Rate Hike May Become Necessary
articles.excerpt: The Bank of Japan board member put the neutral rate near 2%, against today's 1.25%, ahead of a Dec. 18 decision markets expect to bring a hike.
articles.body_md:
Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said Thursday the central bank should be ready to speed up rate increases, and that a half-point hike "may become necessary" if inflation risks build. The policy rate now stands at 1.25%.

In a [speech in Kofu](https://www.boj.or.jp/en/about/press/koen_2026/data/ko261126a1.pdf), Tamura said that because "financial conditions remain accommodative," the bank "needs to bring the policy interest rate to the neutral level soon." He put that neutral level at most likely around 2%, a view he first gave in June.

**What "neutral" means here**

A neutral rate is the level that neither speeds up nor slows the economy. Tamura's estimate leaves about 0.75 percentage point between today's rate and that level. He said Japan's underlying inflation is less firmly anchored at the bank's 2% target, so the bank must respond quickly to signs prices are running above it.

At a news conference after the speech, Tamura said his base case was a quarter-point hike every few months, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/bojs-tamura-signals-chance-of-fasterpace-interest-rate-hikes-5051855). A 50-basis-point move could follow if upside price risks persist, he said, according to Reuters and [Kyodo](https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20261126/p2g/00m/0bu/016000c). A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

He cited oil costs tied to the Middle East conflict, a weaker yen and strong AI-related demand as sources of price pressure.

**December meeting in view**

The BOJ raised its rate to 1.25% from 1% in September, after a hike in June, and held in October. Its next meeting ends Dec. 18, and markets widely expect a quarter-point increase to 1.5%, Reuters and Kyodo reported. Tamura is one of nine board members, and Reuters said markets count him among the board's hawks, meaning members who favor tighter policy. Asked about recent market swings, he said there were about three weeks of data to review before the meeting.

Higher Japanese rates raise the cost of borrowing in yen, which matters to any investor who funds positions abroad with yen loans. Bitcoin traded near $60,460 at 5:53 a.m. ET, up 2.7% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The detail worth chasing is the half-point option. Tamura's own base case is quarter-point moves every few months, so a 50-basis-point step would double that pace and land hardest on anyone funding trades with yen loans. He is one vote of nine, and Dec. 18 is when the full board shows its hand.*

articles.title: Switzerland's First Spot Bitcoin ETF Debuts on SIX With 350 BTC
articles.excerpt: BIT Asset Management's BBIT fund holds bitcoin in Swiss cold storage, charges 0.19% a year and is open only to investors in Switzerland.
articles.body_md:
Switzerland's first spot bitcoin exchange-traded fund began trading on SIX Swiss Exchange on Thursday, holding 350 bitcoin at launch, its sponsor [BIT Asset Management said](https://www.bit.com/pressroom/six-listing).

The Bitcoin Fund ETF, ticker BBIT, trades in Swiss francs and U.S. dollars and charges 0.19% a year, according to [SIX](https://www.six-group.com/en/newsroom/media-releases/2026/20261126-bit-etf-issuer.html) and the issuer, [Pernet von Ballmoos](https://www.pvbswiss.com/en/bitcoin-etf/). Swiss regulator FINMA approved the fund on Oct. 20 after an 18-month review, BIT said.

**A fund instead of a note**

Switzerland has listed bitcoin products for years, but they were exchange-traded products, or ETPs. Those are debt securities, so a buyer holds a claim on the issuer and carries its credit risk. BBIT is an investment fund under Swiss collective investment law. Its bitcoin sits in segregated cold storage, meaning offline wallets, at AMINA Bank, a Swiss bank, segregated from other assets.

SIX said it has listed bitcoin-linked structured products since 2016 and a physically backed single-bitcoin ETP since 2019. BBIT is the exchange's first spot bitcoin ETF, and BIT AM said it is currently Europe's only one.

**Who can buy, and at what price**

The public offering is limited to Switzerland and is not open to U.S. persons, BIT said. Units were issued at $10 when the fund launched on Nov. 19 and listed at $9.26, according to the PvB fund page. PvB classes the fund as an alternative investment with particular risk and says a total loss is possible.

Bitcoin traded near $60,450 at 5:50 a.m. ET, up 2.7% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). BIT said in its release that bitcoin "trades at roughly half its October 2025 high." In the U.S., spot bitcoin ETFs had net outflows of $453 million on Wednesday, per [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/).

Flow Traders is the market maker, and Deloitte audits the fund, BIT said.

*In our opinion: BIT says it is comfortable launching with bitcoin near half its 2025 peak partly because much of the leverage has left the market. Eighteen months of review for one ticker is Swiss thoroughness at work. The real change for Swiss savers is structure: a fund holds the coins for its unitholders, while an ETP buyer is a creditor of the issuer. The number to watch is whether BBIT grows past its 350 starting coins once Swiss banks offer it to clients.*

articles.title: HSBC's RedCoin Stablecoin Passes 100,000 Users in First Month
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong dollar token has about HK$592.8 million in circulation, most of it added in a single week in mid-November, HSBC's own reports show.
articles.body_md:
HSBC's Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin, had more than 100,000 users in its first month, the bank said Thursday, as tokens in circulation stood at about HK$592.8 million (roughly $76 million).

HSBC Hong Kong chief executive Maggie Ng said the figure "shows that interest in HSBC RedCoin is translating into everyday use in the real economy," according to the bank's statement as reported by the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/business/article/3375825/hsbc-sees-more-100000-users-its-stablecoin-first-month-launch) and [The Standard](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/349751/HSBCs-Hong-Kong-dollar-stablecoin-RedCoin-attracts-100000-users). The statement, as reported, did not say how many of those users are active.

**How the coin is backed**

A stablecoin is a token meant to hold a fixed value, here one Hong Kong dollar, by keeping matching reserves. HSBC issues RedCoin under a stablecoin licence from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, and each token can be redeemed one-for-one for Hong Kong dollars, its [RedCoin page](https://www.hsbc.com.hk/stablecoins/) says. The reserves are held in Hong Kong dollar cash.

RedCoin launched in October inside PayMe, HSBC's payment app, which has more than 3.3 million users, SCMP reported. Users can send it to friends or pay at more than 100,000 merchants. Eligible customers can also use it in HSBC's banking app to buy a tokenized class of a Hong Kong dollar money market fund.

**One week drove most of the supply**

HSBC's unaudited weekly statements show circulation of HK$83.2 million on Oct. 28 and HK$91.3 million on Nov. 11. It rose to HK$591.5 million by Nov. 18, an increase of 547.68%, according to the [Nov. 18 statement](https://www.hsbc.com.hk/content/dam/hsbc/hk/docs/mobile/stablecoin/weekly-statement-20261118.pdf). The statement does not give a reason for the jump. The daily figure for Nov. 25 shows a seven-day gain of about HK$1.3 million.

Reserves have exceeded circulation by HK$1 million in each statement. HSBC says its first independent attestation, an outside auditor's check of the reserves, is expected after the fourth quarter of 2026.

Ng said expansion into "broader wealth management and wholesale use cases will proceed in stages."

*In our opinion: The user count measures reach. The balance was built by the roughly HK$500 million that arrived in the week to Nov. 18, and HSBC's statements do not say where it came from. That leaves the first independent attestation, due after the fourth quarter, as the document to read when it lands.*

articles.title: Bank of Korea Raises Rate to 3.25%, Third Hike This Year
articles.excerpt: South Korea's central bank voted 5-2 to lift its base rate a quarter point, citing inflation above target and faster growth driven by chip exports.
articles.body_md:
The Bank of Korea raised its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25% on Thursday, its third increase this year, the central bank [said in its policy statement](https://www.bok.or.kr/eng/bbs/E0000634/view.do?menuNo=400069&nttId=11067086).

The board voted 5-2. Members Hwang Kunil and Lee Soohyung wanted to hold at 3.00%, the statement said. Rates are now at their highest since November 2024, and 32 of 34 analysts in a [Reuters survey](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/south-koreas-central-bank-raises-rates-upgrades-2027-growth-outlook-5051906) expected the move. The bank raised rates in July and August, bringing the total increase to 75 basis points, Reuters reported.

**Why it hiked**

Consumer prices and core prices both rose 2.8% in October from a year earlier, above the bank's 2% target. The bank said inflation will stay above target "for a considerable time" as energy costs pass through. It also raised its growth forecasts to 3.9% for this year and 4.1% for 2027, up from 3.3% and 2.9% in August, on chip exports and investment. It flagged household debt and housing prices in Seoul as financial-stability risks.

**How a rate hike works**

A central bank's base rate is the price of short-term money for banks. When it goes up, loans and mortgages cost more, and savers earn more on deposits. The goal is to cool spending so prices rise more slowly. Higher yields on safe cash also compete with assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin.

The statement now says the board will decide the "timing" of further increases. Before, it said "timing and pace," Reuters reported. Governor Shin Hyun Song told reporters that acting early could mean less tightening in total, and that inflation should return to the 2% target only by the year after next, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/south-koreas-central-bank-raises-rates-upgrades-2027-growth-outlook-5051906).

Bitcoin traded at $60,896 at 11:55 p.m. ET Wednesday, up 3.3% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The two dissents and the dropped word "pace" show a board split on how far to go. For crypto traders, each hike lifts the return on plain cash in won, and bitcoin pays no interest to compete with that. The next test is the bank's first meeting of 2027, where analysts cited by Reuters expect one more quarter-point move.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Reserve Bill With 20-Year Sale Ban Heads to Full House
articles.excerpt: H.R. 8957 would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into law and bar sales for 20 years, but Congress has until Jan. 3 to pass it.
articles.body_md:
A House bill that would put the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into law, and bar the government from selling its bitcoin for at least 20 years, is now cleared for a vote by the full House, according to [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-25-house-committee-advances-strategic-bitcoin-reserve-bill-446778) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/26/strategic-bitcoin-reserve-bill-to-lock-up-u-s-government-held-bitcoin-for-20-years-goes-to-full-house).

The House Financial Services Committee formally reported H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, on Nov. 24. The bill now sits on the House Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789, The Block reported. The committee approved it 28-21 on Sept. 16, with all Republicans voting yes and all Democrats voting no, both outlets reported. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced it on May 21.

**What the bill does**

In short: the bill would direct the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate stockpile for other cryptocurrencies within 180 days of becoming law. Bitcoin placed in the reserve could not be sold, swapped, auctioned or pledged for at least 20 years. Agencies would have to report the digital assets they hold, and the reserve would publish proof-of-reserve reports, both outlets said.

**Why a law matters**

Right now the reserve exists because of President Donald Trump's March 2025 executive order, which fills it mainly with bitcoin the government seized in criminal and civil cases. An executive order can be changed or canceled by a future president. A law can only be undone by Congress. Proof of reserves means publishing evidence, such as wallet addresses, that the coins are really there.

**A short clock**

The 119th Congress ends on Jan. 3, CoinDesk reported. The bill would need a House vote, Senate passage and a signature before then, or be reintroduced next year, when Democrats are set to control both chambers, both outlets reported. On Polymarket, traders priced less than a 5% chance of a national bitcoin reserve being set up by year-end, CoinDesk and The Block reported.

Bitcoin traded at $60,896 at 11:55 p.m. ET Wednesday, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The fight here is over permanence. Lawmakers would turn a reversible order into a 20-year rule, and the bill needs a House vote plus Senate passage in about five weeks that include the holidays. A 20-year holding plan is up against a five-week deadline. Watch the House floor schedule for H.R. 8957 before Jan. 3.*

articles.title: Fidelity Files for Spot Chainlink ETF That Would Skip Staking
articles.excerpt: The proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund would hold LINK through three custodians and list on Nasdaq as FLNK, but its holders would get no staking rewards.
articles.body_md:
Fidelity filed on Wednesday to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund, according to a [Form S-1 registration statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2166611/000119312526477751/d85304ds1.htm) posted on the SEC's EDGAR system. The Fidelity Chainlink Fund would hold LINK directly with three custodians and is expected to trade on Nasdaq.

LINK traded at $9.02 at 5:56 p.m. ET, up 1.7% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/chainlink).

**How the fund would work**

An S-1 is the form a company files to register shares it plans to sell to the public. A spot ETF buys the asset itself, not futures contracts. LINK is the token of Chainlink, an oracle network, meaning a system that feeds outside data such as asset prices into smart contracts, the self-running programs on blockchains. The filing says independent node operators deliver that data, and LINK is the standard unit of payment for their services.

The fund would not stake, which means locking tokens to help secure the network in return for rewards. "The Trust will not stake its LINK, and Shareholders will not receive staking rewards through the Trust," the filing says. It adds that Chainlink staking is capped at about 4% of total supply.

**Who holds the tokens**

Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust and Coinbase Custody would split custody of the fund's LINK. The sponsor is FD Funds Management, a wholly owned unit of FMR LLC, Fidelity's parent. [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-25-fidelity-chainlink-etf-nasdaq-listing-446735) also reported the filing and the three custodians.

Here is the money trail: the fund would pay the sponsor one annual fee, taken as a percentage of its LINK holdings, and that fee covers other service costs. The percentage is still blank in the draft. Shareholders would get LINK's price moves, minus that fee.

**Still a draft**

The filing lists "FLNK" as the expected ticker in brackets, as it does with other details still to be filled in, such as the fee rate and the transfer agent's name. Trading also depends on approval of a Nasdaq application to amend its listing rules, the filing says.

*In our opinion:* Fidelity wants LINK inside a brokerage account but is leaving the staking yield on the table, a trade that keeps the product simple and slightly less generous to holders. Buyers would carry all of LINK's price risk, while the sponsor earns its fee on whatever assets arrive. Watch Nasdaq's listing-rule application, because until it clears, FLNK is a ticker in brackets.

articles.title: Nvidia Agrees to $290 Million Deal Over Crypto Mining Disclosures
articles.excerpt: Shareholders said Nvidia hid how much 2017-2018 gaming chip demand came from crypto miners. The cash deal needs court approval; lawyers seek up to $62 million.
articles.body_md:
Nvidia agreed to pay $290 million in cash to settle a shareholder class action over how it described crypto mining demand for its chips, according to [Bernstein Litowitz Berger & Grossmann](https://www.blbglaw.com/news/updates/2026-11-25-blbg-achieves-290-million-settlement-for-nvidia-investors-after-prevailing-at-us-supreme-court), co-lead counsel for the investors. A motion for preliminary approval was filed Tuesday in federal court in Northern California.

**What investors alleged**

During the 2017-2018 crypto boom, miners bought Nvidia's GeForce graphics cards to run the heavy math that mints new coins. Those sales were booked as gaming revenue. The plaintiffs allege Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang told investors the growth came from gamers, hiding how much rested on volatile mining demand. Their claim on the fallout: when that demand fell in late 2018, the stock dropped 28.5% over two trading sessions.

Nvidia has denied wrongdoing and is not admitting liability under the deal, [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383994/nvidia-290-million-settle-crypto-mining-disclosure-lawsuit) reported. Nvidia said its insurers will fund most of the payment, according to [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-25-nvidia-290-million-settlement-crypto-mining-class-action-446709).

**Seven years in court**

A district judge dismissed the case in 2021. The Ninth Circuit revived it in August 2023, and the Supreme Court in December 2024 dismissed Nvidia's appeal without ruling on the merits, [Kessler Topaz](https://www.ktmc.com/news/kessler-topaz-secures-290-million-settlement-for-nvidia-investors-following-victory-at-u-s-supreme-court/), the other co-lead firm, said. The district court certified the class in March 2026.

**Where the money goes**

The plaintiffs' lawyers plan to ask for up to $62 million of the fund in fees, Decrypt and The Block reported. The rest would go to eligible shareholders after a judge approves the deal and sets a claims process.

The case ran alongside an earlier regulator action. In 2022, Nvidia paid a [$5.5 million SEC penalty](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-79) over its crypto mining disclosures, without admitting or denying the agency's findings.

*In our opinion:* The deal closes a court fight that began with the 2018 mining bust, and it turned on miner purchases that Nvidia booked as gaming revenue. Most of the cost falls on insurers, while lawyers stand to collect about a fifth of the fund. The next step is the judge's ruling on preliminary approval, which starts the clock for shareholders to file claims.

articles.title: French Senate Rejects Crypto Wallet Declaration and Stablecoin Tax
articles.excerpt: Senators turned down three crypto amendments to France's 2027 budget, including a rule to report self-held crypto worth over 100,000 euros and an exit tax.
articles.body_md:
France's Senate on Tuesday rejected three crypto tax amendments to the 2027 budget, including a rule that holders declare self-custodied crypto worth 100,000 euros or more, [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/french-senate-rejects-crypto-exit-tax-stablecoin-swap-tax-and-wallet-declaration-rule/) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/25/french-senate-blocks-new-crypto-tax-and-wallet-list-critics-called-a-kidnapping-risk) reported. Senators also turned down a tax on swaps into stablecoins and a plan to extend France's exit tax to crypto.

**How French crypto tax works now**

Today, trading one crypto for another is not taxed in France. Tax is due when a holder sells for euros or spends crypto on goods. That deferral also covers swaps into stablecoins, tokens pegged to a currency such as the euro or dollar. The amendment from Senator Pascal Savoldelli would have taxed gains on those stablecoin swaps.

Self-custody means holding crypto in a wallet you control, not at an exchange. The declaration rule would have made owners list such holdings (above the 100,000-euro line) with the tax office.

**The government's reasons**

Public Accounts Minister David Amiel opposed the stablecoin tax, saying the tokens are not legal tender, both outlets reported. On the wallet rule, he said a declaration would not help authorities track crypto used in money laundering or tax fraud. He pointed to DAC8, the EU rule that already makes crypto platforms report user data to tax authorities.

CoinDesk reported that some crypto holders had warned a wallet list could expose owners to criminals if the data leaked.

The National Assembly, France's lower house, had approved a stablecoin swap tax in October, both outlets reported. None of the three passed. Current crypto tax rules stay in place for now.

*In our opinion:* For now, French holders keep the right to move into stablecoins without a tax bill, and they avoid a new registry of their self-held coins. The state gives up a revenue source senators wanted, and it relies on DAC8 reporting instead. The 2027 budget is still moving through Parliament, so watch whether any of these measures returns before final passage.

articles.title: PCE Inflation Rises to 3.8% in October as Core Tops Forecast
articles.excerpt: Core PCE rose 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast, as incomes jumped 0.7% and Q3 growth was revised to 4.3%, ahead of the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.
articles.body_md:
U.S. prices rose 3.8% in the 12 months to October on the Fed's preferred gauge, the [Bureau of Economic Analysis](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-october-2026) said at 8:30 a.m. ET Wednesday. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 3.3%.

The core figure came in a tenth of a point above the 3.2% economists expected, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/pce-inflation-report-october-2026.html) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/us-pce-inflation-hits-3-8-core-exceeds-forecast). The Federal Reserve targets 2% inflation, and markets had already priced a quarter-point rate hike for its [Dec. 8-9 meeting](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) before the release, CNBC reported.

**How the PCE gauge works**

The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index tracks what U.S. households pay for goods and services. The "core" version drops food and energy because those prices swing the most. The Fed officially follows the headline number, but policymakers treat core as the better guide to longer-term trends, CNBC noted.

Rates matter for crypto through yield. A higher Fed rate lifts what cash and Treasury bills pay, which raises the bar for assets that pay no interest, such as bitcoin.

**Incomes rose faster than spending**

Personal income rose $201.8 billion, or 0.7%, in October, while spending rose 0.3%, BEA said. CNBC said economists had expected income growth of 0.4%. The saving rate rose to 4.1%, and prices rose 0.3% for the month on both the headline and core measures.

A [separate BEA release](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-second-estimate-and-corporate-profits-3rd-quarter-2026) revised third-quarter growth up 0.9 percentage point, to a 4.3% annual rate, mainly on investment and consumer spending.

**Rate odds for 2027 eased**

Treasury yields fell after the data. Traders still priced two more hikes but cut the odds of a third in 2027 to about 1 in 3, from 50-50 on Tuesday, based on [CME Group's FedWatch](https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html), CNBC reported. "America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said in comments carried by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/25/pce-inflation-report-october-2026.html).

Bitcoin was near $58,230 at 11:49 a.m. ET, down 2.1% over 24 hours, and ether was near $1,635, down 2.2%, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The number that matters for December is 3.3%, the core reading that came in above forecasts. With a hike already priced, the Dec. 9 statement and the Fed's new projections carry the real information. The next PCE report lands Dec. 23, two weeks after that meeting.*

articles.title: Ukraine Passes Crypto Law Setting 23% Tax on Investor Gains
articles.excerpt: Lawmakers expect 15 billion hryvnias, about $331 million, in new revenue. Rules start July 1, 2027, and the central bank will oversee stablecoins.
articles.body_md:
Ukraine's parliament passed a law on Wednesday that legalizes the country's crypto market and taxes individuals' gains at 23%, with 271 lawmakers voting in favor, [Ukrinform](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-economy/4188437-ukraines-parliament-passes-law-to-legalize-cryptocurrency.html) reported.

Yaroslav Zhelezniak, first deputy chair of the Verkhovna Rada's finance, tax and customs committee, said the law should add 15 billion hryvnias to budget revenue. That is about $331 million at the [National Bank of Ukraine's](https://bank.gov.ua/en/markets/exchangerates) official rate. The rules take effect July 1, 2027.

**How the tax works**

Individuals will pay 18% personal income tax plus a 5% military levy on crypto profits, Ukrinform reported. Swapping one crypto asset for another is not taxed, and losses can be carried forward to later years.

Coins bought before the law takes effect get a transition rate when holders cash out to hryvnias or other traditional money in 2027 and 2028: 5% plus the 5% levy. Zhelezniak wrote on [Telegram](https://t.me/yzheleznyak/20776) that this lower rate applies to the full amount cashed out, not only the gain. After 2028, the standard 18% plus 5% applies.

In plain terms, a holder who cashes out 100,000 hryvnias during the transition owes 10,000 hryvnias, whatever the original cost. Under the standard rate, the same holder owes 23% of the profit only.

**Central bank gets stablecoins**

Oversight will be split between the National Securities and Stock Market Commission and the National Bank of Ukraine, according to Ukrinform and [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/383962/ukraine-passes-law-to-legalize-and-tax-its-crypto-market-from-july-2027). The central bank will handle stablecoins, tokens pegged to a currency such as the dollar, and can allow or ban their circulation.

The bill, No. 10225-d, was recommended for final passage by the finance committee on Nov. 4, Ukrinform reported. Zhelezniak said it took three years of working groups. The law still needs the president's signature, Decrypt reported.

*In our opinion: The question worth chasing is who pays more under the transition rate. Ten percent of the full amount costs less than 23% of the profit only when the gain is about 43% or more of the cash-out, so the lower rate is lower only for holders with large gains. The next step to watch is the president's signature, then July 1, 2027.*

articles.title: EBA Asks EU to Weigh Rules for Crypto Firms Offering DeFi Lending
articles.excerpt: An EBA report says some crypto firms market DeFi lending as a way to earn on stablecoins, though MiCA bans interest on e-money tokens.
articles.body_md:
The European Banking Authority on Wednesday asked the European Commission to assess whether crypto firms that steer clients into decentralized finance (DeFi), especially lending protocols, need extra rules, in a [report](https://www.eba.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-11/33382389-2e75-4da8-845c-4201664befe9/Report%20on%20use%20of%20EMTs%20and%20other%20stablecoins%20in%20decentralised%20finance.pdf) on stablecoins in DeFi.

The EBA said it found evidence that some crypto-asset service providers, the exchanges and brokers licensed under the EU's MiCA law, market DeFi access as a way for users to "earn" on stablecoins. MiCA bans issuers and those firms from paying interest on e-money tokens (EMTs), stablecoins tied to one official currency such as the euro.

**How the yield route works**

DeFi lending protocols are blockchain apps that pool deposits and lend them to borrowers without a company in the middle. A stablecoin holder who deposits earns the interest borrowers pay. That is the yield. MiCA leaves out services run "in a fully decentralised manner," the [EBA said](https://www.eba.europa.eu/publications-and-media/press-releases/eba-examines-use-stablecoins-including-emts-decentralised-finance), so the protocol sits outside the law while the licensed firm that routes a customer there does not.

**Options on the table**

In its earlier response to the Commission's MiCA review, the EBA listed possible measures for firms that offer this access:

- suitability tests and extra risk disclosures
- leverage limits
- a ban on routing clients through DeFi to stablecoins not authorized under MiCA
- a certification regime for DeFi lending protocols

The report names Tether's USDT among stablecoins with no MiCA authorization, which means it cannot be offered to the EU public. A 2026 survey cited by the EBA found 15% of people surveyed in Western Europe held it anyway.

**EU use is small but growing**

Germany, France and Spain lead the EU in DeFi activity but rank 18th, 19th and 26th worldwide, the report said, citing Chainalysis. It also cited a survey in which 42% of European-based investors expect to use DeFi by 2028. Assets locked in DeFi protocols stood near $67.2 billion on Wednesday, according to [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/).

The Commission has not said whether it will add such rules in its MiCA review, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/25/eu-bank-watchdog-seeks-european-commission-rules-for-crypto-firms-offering-defi-lending) reported.

*In our opinion: The stake here is the on-ramp. Rules aimed at firms that route customers into DeFi would land on licensed exchanges and brokers, the one link in the chain EU supervisors already reach. The decision point is the Commission's MiCA review, and the EBA says it will keep feeding that review with evidence through 2027.*

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Lose $231 Million, Sixth Straight Day of Outflows
articles.excerpt: Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $231.4 million on Tuesday, the smallest of six straight outflow days. IBIT led again; three funds took in money.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost a net $231.4 million on Tuesday, their sixth straight day of outflows, pushing November's total to $4.94 billion, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data show.

It was also the smallest withdrawal of the six. Monday's was $569.7 million, and last Friday's $669.2 million was the month's largest.

**BlackRock's fund again led the exits**

- BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT): $175.3 million out
- Fidelity's FBTC: $44.0 million out
- Ark's ARKB: $15.8 million out
- Bitwise's BITB: $10.3 million out
- Franklin's EZBC, Grayscale's Bitcoin Mini Trust and Morgan Stanley's MSBT took in a combined $14.0 million

SoSoValue, a second data provider, put the day at $231.56 million in net outflows, [TokenPost](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/investing/62501) reported, and counted the same six-day streak.

A spot bitcoin ETF holds actual bitcoin. When investors redeem more shares than they buy, the fund hands back or sells bitcoin to pay them, and that net figure is the "outflow." These funds have been trading since January 2024.

**A monthly record, now bigger**

November's $4.94 billion is the largest monthly outflow in Farside's records, above June 2026's $4.51 billion. Fifteen of the month's 17 trading days have been negative. Net inflows since launch still total about $52.1 billion, Farside's figures show.

Total net assets across the funds stood at $72.01 billion, about 5.99% of bitcoin's market value, according to SoSoValue data cited by TokenPost.

Bitcoin traded at $58,852 at 5:54 a.m. ET, down 0.95% over 24 hours, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show.

*In our opinion: A smaller outflow is still an outflow, and the November tally grows with each red day. Even so, about $52.1 billion of net money is still in these funds, so the month has taken back less than a tenth of what came in before it. The next figure is Wednesday's: an inflow would be the funds' first since Nov. 16, when they took in $7.9 million.*

articles.title: SBI, SMFG and Solana Foundation Launch Japan Stablecoin Venture
articles.excerpt: SBI Solana Global, formerly SBI R3 Japan, will build stablecoin payments and tokenized bonds and funds on Solana, starting in Japan. Stakes weren't disclosed.
articles.body_md:
SBI Holdings, Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) and the Solana Foundation said Wednesday their joint venture, SBI Solana Global, has started full operations. The Solana-based firm is backed by two groups with $2.3 trillion in combined assets, the foundation said.

The company already existed. It is SBI R3 Japan under a new name and ownership setup, according to the [joint announcement](https://www.sbigroup.co.jp/english/news/pdf/2026/1125_a_en.pdf). The three partners said they completed a series of agreements for the change, which SBI first laid out on July 13, [crypto.news](https://crypto.news/sbi-solana-global-launch-japan-onchain-finance/) reported. The release did not disclose ownership stakes or what any party paid.

**Four lines of business**

The venture listed four areas:

- Payment rails: stablecoin transfers inside Japan and across borders, including small payments made by AI agents.
- Tokenized financial assets: bonds, investment funds and loan receivables.
- Tokenized real-world assets: commodities and other rights, with records that track authenticity.
- On-chain asset management built on stablecoins and tokenized assets.

A stablecoin is a token built to track a set value, such as one yen or one dollar. "Tokenizing" a bond means recording ownership on a blockchain, so it can be traded and settled outside normal banking hours.

**The $2.3 trillion belongs to the parent groups**

The Solana Foundation said SBI and SMFG have more than $2.3 trillion in combined assets and over 80 million customers, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-11-25-japans-sbi-smfg-tap-solana-stablecoin-tokenization-joint-venture-446131) reported. Crypto.news noted those figures describe the size of the two groups. The release named no assets moving to Solana and gave no launch dates, products or revenue targets.

The partners said they "will first establish practical use cases and a solid business foundation in Japan," then expand across Asia.

SBI R3 Japan was set up in 2019 and earlier worked on R3's Corda blockchain software for companies, crypto.news reported.

Solana's SOL token traded at $67.69 at 5:54 a.m. ET, down 3.4% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

*In our opinion: A Japanese megabank group now has its name on a company built on a public blockchain, a different bet from the enterprise Corda work this firm did before. The money at risk sits with the three partners, and none of their stakes are public. The first thing to watch is a named product with a launch date and a size attached.*

articles.title: Hong Kong Launches Blockchain Bond Platform With 10 Banks
articles.excerpt: The HKMA's CMU Digital Asset Platform settles tokenized bonds 24 hours a day with cash tokens. Links to regulated stablecoins are planned but not yet live.
articles.body_md:
Hong Kong's de facto central bank on Wednesday launched a blockchain-based platform for issuing and settling bonds, with 10 banks, including HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China (Hong Kong), signed up as the first direct participants.

The [Hong Kong Monetary Authority](https://www.hkma.gov.hk/eng/news-and-media/press-releases/2026/11/20261125-3/) (HKMA) said the CMU Digital Asset Platform, or CMU DAP, handles a bond's whole life on a shared ledger: issuance, settlement of trades, coupon payments and repayment at maturity. It can also turn existing bonds into tokens.

**Bond and cash move in one step**

The platform runs on distributed ledger technology, a database that several institutions share and update together. It settles by "atomic delivery versus payment": the bond and the cash change hands in one step, or not at all. Cash on the ledger takes the form of "cash tokens," and the HKMA said the system connects directly to real-time gross settlement systems (where banks settle large payments one by one) and central bank digital currencies. It runs 24 hours a day. It handles several currencies.

The Central Moneymarkets Unit (CMU) is Hong Kong's existing depository for debt securities. It is run by CMU OmniClear, an operator set up in October 2024. [CMU OmniClear said](https://www.cmuomniclear.com/en/news-and-events/id/3941) trial trades in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, short-term HKMA debt, tested the platform earlier this year.

**Stablecoin links come later, with no date**

CMU OmniClear said it will "explore" adding funds and real-world assets and linking the platform to tokenized deposits and regulated stablecoins. Neither release set a date for that, named a first bond issue on the system or listed fees.

CMU OmniClear's release lists the other seven: Bank of Communications (Hong Kong), China CITIC Bank International, China Construction Bank (Asia), CMB Wing Lung Bank, Crédit Agricole CIB, DBS Bank's Hong Kong branch and Industrial Bank. [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-25-hong-kong-debt-securities-tokenization-446132) also reported the launch and the 10-bank first batch.

"CMU OmniClear is implementing a strategic roadmap to establish the CMU as the core infrastructure for a multi-asset digital financial ecosystem in Hong Kong," HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said in the statement.

*In our opinion: Earlier this year this was a trial with HKMA bills. Now it is part of the city's official bond depository, with 10 banks connected on day one. The number worth chasing is the size of the first live bond issue on CMU DAP, and the first trade settled with a licensed stablecoin.*

articles.title: Stablecoin Supply Drops $17.2 Billion in a Month, Most Since 2022
articles.excerpt: Tether's USDT shrank about $8 billion as holders redeemed tokens for dollars, while bitcoin fell about 26% over the same 30 days, data show.
articles.body_md:
Stablecoin supply fell $17.2 billion in the 30 days to Nov. 24, a 5.7% drop to $283.2 billion, according to [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) data.

That is the biggest 30-day decline in DefiLlama's records outside May 2022, when TerraUSD lost its peg and about $28.6 billion left in a month. [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/stablecoin-supply-fell-more-than-17-billion-in-a-month-at-past-turns-it-moved-after-bitcoin/) made the same comparison on Tuesday.

Many traders treat stablecoin supply as "dry powder," or cash waiting to buy crypto, [Unchained wrote](https://unchainedcrypto.com/stablecoin-supply-fell-more-than-17-billion-in-a-month-at-past-turns-it-moved-after-bitcoin/). A smaller pile means fewer dollars sitting one step from a purchase.

**How supply shrinks**

A stablecoin is a token designed to stay worth $1. When a holder returns tokens to the issuer for ordinary dollars, called a redemption, the issuer burns them, taking them out of circulation, and supply falls. When someone deposits dollars, new tokens are minted. So a falling total means more money left through the issuer's door than came in.

**Tether's USDT led the decline**

Tether's USDT, the largest stablecoin, shrank about $8.0 billion over the month to $174.2 billion, DefiLlama's dashboard showed late Tuesday. Circle's USDC fell $2.7 billion to $69.0 billion. Sky's USDS dropped about $3.5 billion to $3.2 billion, more than half its supply.

Not every token shrank. Ethena's USDe added about $310 million and Ripple's RLUSD about $340 million.

By blockchain, Ethereum carried most of the drop: stablecoin supply there fell $13.9 billion, to $129.5 billion, DefiLlama's chain data show.

Bitcoin moved the same way over the period. It traded near $80,000 on Oct. 26 and at $58,933 at 11:53 p.m. ET Tuesday, a drop of about 26%, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). The data show both fell together. They don't show which moved first.

*In our opinion: The number that matters is $174.2 billion, the USDT pool that has carried nearly half of this month's exits. Supply ticked up on Nov. 23 and Nov. 24 before slipping again, so the next weekly reading on DefiLlama will show whether redemptions are still running. Stablecoins are built to sit still at $1; this month, a good share of them sat the market out.*

articles.title: Australia's Inflation Rises to 4.9% in October as Fuel Jumps 6.3%
articles.excerpt: Core inflation rose to 3.8%, above the RBA's 2% to 3% target, as electricity costs climbed 25.2% after government rebates ended, the ABS said.
articles.body_md:
Australia's consumer prices rose 4.9% in the 12 months to October, up from 4.3% in September, the [Australian Bureau of Statistics](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/economy/price-indexes-and-inflation/consumer-price-index-australia/latest-release) said at 7:30 p.m. ET Tuesday.

Prices rose 0.5% in October alone, above the 0.4% forecast, [Reuters reported](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/australian-inflation-heats-up-in-october-core-hits-twoyear-high-5049563). The trimmed mean, a core gauge, rose to 3.8% from 3.6%, its fastest pace since 2024.

**Why core and headline differ**

The Consumer Price Index tracks what households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services. The trimmed mean drops the items with the biggest price moves each month, up or down, so one spike can't swing it. In October the ABS said automotive fuel was left out of the trimmed mean, a main reason it sits more than a point below the headline rate.

**Power bills and petrol drove the jump**

Housing costs rose 6.4% over the year, led by a 25.2% rise in electricity. "The rise in electricity reflects Commonwealth government rebates, which reduced household electricity costs last year but are no longer in place," ABS head of price statistics Rachael McCririck said in a [release](https://www.abs.gov.au/media-centre/media-releases/cpi-rose-49-year-october-2026).

Transport rose 10.6%. Fuel was up 32.5% over the year and 6.3% in October, on higher world oil prices, the ABS said.

**Economists split on the next step**

The Reserve Bank of Australia targets inflation of 2% to 3% and has raised rates by 125 basis points this year, Reuters reported. Westpac chief economist Luci Ellis said she expects October to be the peak and sees "nothing to change our view that the RBA is likely finished hiking rates." Krishna Bhimavarapu of State Street Investment Management said persistent inflation "may ultimately require policy to become more restrictive."

After the release, the Australian dollar rose 0.1% to $0.6650, and traders cut the odds of a June rate cut to about 75% from nearly fully priced, Reuters reported. Bitcoin was at $58,933 at 11:53 p.m. ET, down 2.3% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The figure the RBA board will study is 3.8%, not 4.9%. Fuel sat outside the trimmed mean this month, so the core rise came without help from petrol, and that is the reading the two camps are arguing over. The board announces its next decision on Dec. 8, and November's CPI follows on Jan. 6.*

articles.title: Utah Moves to Drop Kalshi Criminal Case After Company Exits State
articles.excerpt: Utah's motion is without prejudice, so all 14 charges can be refiled if Kalshi returns. Kalshi's top lawyer said jurisdiction disputes should not be criminalized.
articles.body_md:
Utah's attorney general has moved to dismiss all 14 criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and its two co-founders after the company blocked Utah users. The [Utah Attorney General's Office](https://attorneygeneral.utah.gov/utah-dismiss-kalshi-criminal-case/) said Tuesday it filed the motion in the Third District Court on Monday, the day Kalshi said it was pausing operations in Utah.

The dismissal is without prejudice, so prosecutors can refile the charges if Kalshi resumes offering its markets in the state, the office said. Co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara had been due in court on Dec. 4, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/24/utah-drops-charges-against-kalshi-after-it-halted-operations-in-state.html) reported, citing court documents. [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/utah-drops-criminal-case-against-kalshi-after-prediction-market-exits-state-5048877) also reported the arraignment was set for next week.

**Gambling charges filed Oct. 28**

The charges, filed Oct. 28, centered on promoting online gambling, according to the [Salt Lake Tribune](https://www.sltrib.com/news/2026/11/24/after-kalshi-pulls-out-utah-state/) and Reuters. The office alleges Kalshi was offering gambling to Utah residents, its release said.

"Utah does not allow gambling, and prediction markets are gambling," Attorney General Derek Brown said in the office's release. "Kalshi has pulled out of Utah, and if it returns, so will the charges."

"Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized," Kalshi general counsel Yaakov Roth said in a statement quoted by the Tribune.

**A fight over who sets the rules**

A prediction market lets users trade contracts that pay out if an event happens, such as a team winning or a candidate being elected. Kalshi argues these event contracts fall under the exclusive oversight of the federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and the CFTC shares that view, Reuters reported. Utah says they are gambling, which its constitution bars.

The CFTC sued Utah the day before the state announced its charges, CNBC reported. A federal judge heard arguments in that case on Friday and has not ruled, Reuters reported. Utah's separate civil case against Kalshi continues, Reuters and the Tribune reported.

Brown's office said seven prediction market companies, including Kalshi, have agreed to stop operating in Utah.

*In our opinion: The criminal case is off the table, but the dispute that produced it is not. Utah keeps its civil suit and the option to refile, so any return by Kalshi now runs through the courts, starting with the federal judge's ruling in the CFTC's case. That ruling will matter to every platform that wants to list sports contracts in Utah.*

articles.title: SEC Staff Grant Molecule No-Action Relief for Research Tokens
articles.excerpt: The Nov. 24 staff letter covers tokens from Molecule's U.S. unit LabsCo that fund biotech research and carry advisory votes but no equity or profit rights.
articles.body_md:
SEC staff said Tuesday they will not recommend enforcement action if Molecule's U.S. subsidiary sells tokens that fund scientific research without registering them as securities. The Nov. 24 response, from the Division of Corporation Finance, answered a request Molecule's lawyers filed on Nov. 19, according to [Jurelist](https://jurelist.com/news/sec-staff-will-not-recommend-enforcement-against-labsco-over-project-token-sales-3dc659e6) and [The Crypto Times](https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/11/25/sec-offers-molecule-limited-enforcement-relief-for-project-token-sales/).

Deputy Chief Counsel Jonathan A. Ingram signed it.

The letter covers both the token sale itself and LabsCo's decision not to register the tokens as a class of equity securities, both outlets reported. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/regulation/sec-staff-give-molecule-no-action-relief-for-token-sales) also reported the relief.

**What a no-action letter does**

A no-action letter is SEC staff saying they would not ask the commission to bring a case if a company does exactly what it described. It is not a commission vote. The staff said the position rests on the facts Molecule presented, that different facts could change the answer, and that it expresses no legal conclusion, according to Jurelist and The Crypto Times.

**Votes on research, no share of profits**

Molecule AG is a Swiss company that has led development of a blockchain-based protocol for funding biotech research since 2018, according to the [request letter](https://www.sec.gov/files/corpfin/no-action/molecule-ag-nal-111926.pdf) from law firm Cahill Gordon & Reindel. Its Delaware subsidiary, LabsCo, would sell "Project Tokens" for cash or crypto and also hand them out as airdrops and as rewards for tasks such as reviewing research proposals or contributing data.

Sale proceeds would fund the research. Holders who lock their tokens can cast advisory votes on research direction, which LabsCo does not have to follow, the letter says. The tokens carry no equity, debt or profit rights and no right to buy shares in any later LabsCo stock offering, which would be run separately under securities law.

The request leans on the SEC's March 17, 2026 interpretive guidance, which sorts crypto assets into five groups and says "digital tools" such as memberships and credentials are not securities, the letter says. It does not say how many tokens LabsCo plans to sell or at what price. Molecule told the SEC it expects to form more subsidiaries under the same model.

articles.excerpt: CleanSpark's revenue fell 25% to $576.5 million as it mined 8% fewer coins, while its Georgia site signed a 20-year, $6.6 billion data center lease.
articles.body_md:
CleanSpark lost $987.1 million in the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, after a $364.5 million profit a year earlier, the bitcoin miner said Tuesday in its [results release](https://investors.cleanspark.com/news/news-details/2026/CleanSpark-Reports-Fiscal-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2026-Financial-and-Operating-Results/default.aspx) and [annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827876/000119312526476040/clsk-20260930.htm).

Revenue fell 25% to $576.5 million. In the fourth quarter alone, revenue dropped 46% to $120.9 million, though the company posted net income of $9.8 million for the quarter.

**A $281.6 million bitcoin markdown**

CleanSpark recorded a $281.6 million loss on the fair value of its bitcoin, compared with a $425.6 million gain the year before. The annual report ties that to bitcoin falling from about $114,100 to about $83,600 between the two fiscal year-ends. It also booked a $118.7 million loss on bitcoin pledged as collateral and $177.1 million in impairment charges, mostly tied to converting its Sandersville, Georgia, site from mining to data center use.

Under fair-value accounting, a company marks the bitcoin it holds to market each quarter, so a lower price shows up as a loss even if no coins are sold. An impairment is a write-down of equipment or property the company no longer expects to earn as much from.

**Fewer coins mined, a long lease signed**

CleanSpark mined 7,253 bitcoin in the year, down 8%, as its average hashrate, the computing power it points at the network, fell 21% to 36.0 exahashes per second. It held 13,530 bitcoin, including collateral, worth $1.1 billion on Sept. 30.

The Sandersville site now has a 20-year, $6.6 billion lease with a tenant the company called "high investment grade" without naming it. CleanSpark funded construction with $2.276 billion of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031 and plans its first data hall for November 2027.

CleanSpark shares closed at $5.10 on Tuesday, down 7.8%, before the results came out, according to [Nasdaq](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/clsk). Bitcoin traded near $59,995 at 5:48 p.m. ET, down 1.7% over 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), with [Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/price/bitcoin) showing $59,970.

*In our opinion: The bigger story sits in Georgia. Spread evenly, the $6.6 billion over 20 years averages about $330 million a year, more than half of what mining brought in during fiscal 2026. Much of the loss was a paper markdown on coins the company still holds, and at Tuesday's price those 13,530 bitcoin would be worth about $812 million. The date to watch is November 2027, when the first data hall is due.*

articles.title: Ethereum Foundation Makes Quantum, AI Defense Top Priority
articles.excerpt: The EF doubled its protocol security team and backs hash-based keys to replace elliptic curves, with 2029 as its internal deadline and other upgrades on hold.
articles.body_md:
The Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and made protecting Ethereum from quantum computers and AI its top priority, with a 2029 internal deadline, the nonprofit said in a [blog post](https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/11/23/pqai-0) published Monday.

The post, by EF's Kev Wedderburn, said AI has become the more urgent risk because models already find software bugs faster than people can review them.

**What changes, in plain words**

Ethereum accounts and validators prove who they are with digital signatures built on elliptic-curve math. That math is considered hard to break today. A large enough quantum computer, or a mathematical shortcut, could let someone forge those signatures.

After more than a year of testing options, the EF backs hash-based cryptography as the replacement. Hash functions turn data into a fixed-length fingerprint, and Ethereum already relies on them, so the switch "does not add a new assumption," the post said.

The plan has three parts:

- Validators, which propose and vote on blocks, would sign with hash-based keys.
- Wallets would give users a simple way to move their accounts to hash-based signatures.
- Blobs, the data batches rollups post to Ethereum, would switch to hash-based commitments.

**The cost**

Other planned features will wait. Core developers will use their remaining calls this year to decide what else to cut from Hegotá, an upcoming upgrade, and Ethlabs has pulled its Quick Slots proposal for faster blocks to free up engineers, the EF and [Unchained](https://unchainedcrypto.com/ethereum-foundation-puts-quantum-and-ai-threats-first-doubles-its-protocol-security-team/) reported.

Much larger signatures mean the EF will watch hardware needs so people can still run nodes at home, and wallets, multisigs and staking pools all need changes. The foundation called the job harder than the Merge, Ethereum's switch to proof-of-stake on Sept. 15, 2022, "and we have less time."

Researcher Justin Drake proposed December 2028 as a target at Devcon, while 2029 stays the internal deadline until a timeline review in January, the EF said.

Ether traded at $1,671 at 11:55 a.m. ET, down 5.3% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/ethereum).

*In our opinion: The EF's own sign-off says the Merge changed the engine in flight and this time it changes the locks, which is a fair summary with one catch: every wallet holder eventually has to pick up a new key. The stake is user funds, and the risk sits with accounts that never migrate. The January timeline review is the next date to circle.*

articles.title: HSBC, JPMorgan, StoneX Settle First Live Pooled-Gold Trades in London
articles.excerpt: The World Gold Council pilot let banks own, trade and pledge fractions of vaulted bars. ICE's benchmark unit ran it as the FCA weighs tokenized gold rules.
articles.body_md:
HSBC, JPMorgan and StoneX traded fractions of 400-ounce London gold bars and pledged them as collateral without moving the metal, the [World Gold Council](https://www.gold.org/news-and-events/press-releases/world-gold-council-facilitates-first-live-transactions-using-pooled) said Tuesday.

They were the first live, legally binding deals under the council's new system and settled on Nov. 17, according to law firm [Linklaters](https://www.linklaters.com/about-us/news-and-deals/deals/2026/november/linklaters-advises-world-gold-council-on-successful-wholesale-digital-gold-pilot), which advised the council. The banks did not disclose how much gold changed hands, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/business/2026/11/24/jpmorgan-hsbc-and-stonex-complete-first-digital-gold-trades-in-london) reported.

**How the new gold claim works**

London's gold market holds metal in two main ways. "Allocated" gold means you own specific, numbered bars. "Unallocated" gold is cheaper and easier to trade, but it is only a contract with a bank, so the holder is exposed if that bank fails.

The new instrument, called Pooled Gold Interests, tries to offer both. Standard 400-ounce bars go into a pool, and holders get an ownership interest in that pool that can be split into fractions of an ounce and moved electronically, Linklaters said. In the pilot, the bars were placed in the system, traded and used as collateral, then withdrawn after settlement, the council said.

ICE Benchmark Administration, part of Intercontinental Exchange, ran the system, and Baton Systems supplied the technology, according to the council and [Mining.com](https://www.mining.com/world-gold-council-brings-digital-gold-trading-to-life/).

Mark Amlin, JPMorgan's global head of physical commodities, said in the council's release that gold that is "fractional, readily transferable and insolvency remote" could be used more widely, including as collateral.

**Still a pilot**

The project is at the pilot stage and is meant to sit alongside existing settlement methods. Governance rules and a timetable for wider use have not been finalized, CoinDesk reported. The pilot comes as the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority reviews responses to its call for input on tokenized gold in wholesale markets, the council said.

Crypto already has its own version. Gold-backed tokens had a combined market value of about $4.96 billion as of 11:48 a.m. ET Tuesday, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/tokenized-gold). PAX Gold traded at $3,559, down 2.6% over 24 hours, at 11:55 a.m. ET, CoinGecko data show.

*In our opinion: This is a bank-run answer to the problem gold tokens set out to solve, owning real bars in small pieces that can move quickly. The difference is who stands in the middle: a pool operated by ICE's benchmark unit rather than a single token issuer. The next marker is the FCA's response to its call for input on tokenized gold, including its use as collateral.*

articles.title: Nasdaq Jumps 6.5% After Nvidia Reinstates Huang as CEO
articles.excerpt: The Nasdaq had its best day since April 2025 and recovered just over half of last week's S&P 500 drop. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $569.7 million on Monday, after $1.79 billion in the week through Friday.
articles.body_md:
The Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.51% on Monday, its best day since April 2025, after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. The index closed at 24,089.56, per [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/22/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) and [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/). The S&P 500 gained 4.73% to 7,237.17, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1,447.98 points, or 3.01%, to 49,595.31, [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/22/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-rates-technology-ai-anthropic-49ba1beba78fa4ed2bd5898029f79c91) reported. [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261124/371a820ce169433abdb1e4e51c6dbfbe/c.html) published the same official closes.

This midweek note covers the stretch from Friday's close on Nov. 20 to Monday's close on Nov. 23, after our [November "Where the Money Went" deep dive](https://blackmint.markets/news/where-the-money-went-november-deep-dive). Last week the Nasdaq fell 10% and the S&P 500 fell 8.6%, per Yahoo Finance data. Monday's bounce recovered just over half of that S&P 500 drop, the [AP](https://apnews.com/article/stocks-markets-rates-technology-ai-anthropic-49ba1beba78fa4ed2bd5898029f79c91) reported. Overnight stock futures were already firmer after authorities in Asia moved to steady their markets, as we [reported Monday morning](https://blackmint.markets/news/nasdaq-futures-rebound-asia-market-support). The Nvidia news then sent U.S. cash indexes sharply higher. For how the board reversed course, see our [deep dive on Huang's reinstatement](https://blackmint.markets/news/nvidia-reinstates-huang-ceo).

**The Friday-to-Monday scoreboard**

Change from Friday's close to Monday's close, from Yahoo Finance data, with the major indexes also checked against CNBC and AP or Xinhua. Bitcoin and ether are compared at 4 p.m. ET both days, using [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) and Yahoo Finance:

- Technology fund (XLK): up 9.0%
- Ether: up 7.8%
- Nasdaq Composite: up 6.5%
- Bitcoin: up 5.0%
- S&P 500: up 4.7%
- Gold futures: up 3.9%
- Dow: up 3.0%
- U.S. dollar index: up 0.5%
- Consumer staples fund (XLP): down 0.1%
- WTI crude oil: down 3.9%

Those crypto gains are from Friday's cash close through Monday's. They include a weekend bounce. They do not mean bitcoin kept pace with stocks on Monday itself.

**How it works: prices can rebound without new measured flows**

A rising price does not, by itself, tell you that a pile of new cash arrived. Every buy still has a seller, so the cash only changes hands. If the Nasdaq jumps 6.5%, holders gain value on paper. Flows are different. They count dollars that actually moved into or out of a fund, a stablecoin or a share sale. That is why this story tracks both, and why some figures below still cover Friday or the week through Friday, when the complete reports are in.

**Nvidia and the sector turn**

Nvidia shares closed at $165.05, up $39.52, or 31.48%, from Friday's close of $125.53, per [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/) and [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/23/tech-sell-off-ai-stock-market-support-measures-deployed-south-korea-taiwan-china-ftse-nasdaq-latest-news-updates). [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Dollar+climbs+as+renewed+AI+euphoria+fuels+Fed+hike+bets/27389508.html), via StreetInsider, said the move added roughly $950 billion to Nvidia's market value. The Guardian put the increase at $952 billion, from $3.03 trillion on Friday to $3.977 trillion.

The technology sector led the rebound. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK) rose 8.97% to $162.38, per Yahoo Finance. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) said the S&P 500 technology sector soared 9%, and [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261124/371a820ce169433abdb1e4e51c6dbfbe/c.html) put it at up 9.03%. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sectors finished higher. Energy and consumer staples were the laggards; the matching funds, XLE and XLP, closed down 1.06% and 0.09% on Yahoo Finance.

**Bitcoin bounced over the weekend, then sat out Monday's stock rally**

Bitcoin was about $58,300 at 4 p.m. ET Friday and about $61,192 at 4 p.m. ET Monday, up 5.0%, per CoinGecko, with Yahoo Finance's 4 p.m. hour closes showing a similar 4.9% rise. Ether rose 7.8% over the same window, from about $1,599 to about $1,724.

The path was not a straight line. CoinGecko hourly data show bitcoin near $55,700 early Saturday. It then recovered, and it traded around $63,700 on Monday morning as the Nvidia news hit, matching the move we recorded in [Monday's deep dive](https://blackmint.markets/news/nvidia-reinstates-huang-ceo). By the 4 p.m. equity close it was back near $61,200. [The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/23/crypto-market-today-nov-23-bitcoin-sits-out-wall-street-s-historic-rally-as-usd1-8-billion-etf-exodus-weighs-on-prices/) similarly described bitcoin as little changed on Monday itself while the Nasdaq surged 6.51%.

**The dollar, Treasuries, gold and oil**

The U.S. dollar index closed at 104.32, up 0.49% from Friday's 103.81, per Yahoo Finance. [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Dollar+climbs+as+renewed+AI+euphoria+fuels+Fed+hike+bets/27389508.html) said the dollar firmed at 104.32 and had peaked at 104.53 on Monday. The Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP) rose 0.54%.

The 10-year Treasury yield was little changed, closing at 4.918% on Yahoo Finance's ^TNX series after Friday's 4.912%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/treasury-yields-bonds-fed.html) had the 10-year near 4.93% during the session. The 7-10 year Treasury fund IEF was flat, down less than 0.02%.

Gold futures rose 3.9% to $3,651.40, per Yahoo Finance. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/gold-rises-from-14-month-low-as-markets-await-us-inflation-data.html) had U.S. gold futures at $3,649, up 3.8%, and spot gold at $3,650.62, up 3.4%, as of about 1:35 p.m. ET.

West Texas Intermediate crude for January delivery settled at $80.17 a barrel, down $3.24, or 3.88%. Brent for January settled at $89.37, down $3.20, or 3.46%, [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20261124/5bc9039da7b947e9a17527c6233595f8/c.html) reported. Yahoo Finance showed the same settlement prices.

**What the flow reports show**

The complete flow prints show money leaving spot crypto ETFs last week, and again on Monday, even as prices bounced after Friday's close.

U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.790 billion of net outflows in the week of Nov. 16 to Nov. 20, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show. [SoSoValue data reported by Bitcoin.com](https://news.bitcoin.com/bitcoin-etf/bitcoin-etfs-lose-1-79b-in-3rd-largest-weekly-outflow/) also put the weekly total at $1.79 billion. [Bloomingbit](https://en.bloomingbit.io/feed/news/125009), also citing SoSoValue, published the same weekly figure.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $1,367.5 million of that week, or about 76% of the total, per Farside. SoSoValue via Bitcoin.com put IBIT at $1.37 billion, and Bloomingbit put it at $1.368 billion. The rest of the week's fund tally, published by Farside and, with only small rounding differences, by Bitcoin.com from SoSoValue and by [Trading Notified](https://tradingnotified.com/markets/bitcoin-etfs-1-79-billion-weekly-outflow/) from Farside's daily prints, was:

- Fidelity's Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC): $198.9 million out
- Grayscale Bitcoin Trust (GBTC): $119.3 million out
- ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB): $68.0 million out
- Bitwise Bitcoin ETF (BITB): $43.6 million out
- Grayscale Bitcoin Mini Trust (BTC): $28.9 million out
- Morgan Stanley's Bitcoin Trust (MSBT): $53.3 million in, the week's largest inflow

Smaller funds added a further net outflow. WisdomTree's BTCW took in $0.3 million, per Farside and Trading Notified.

Friday, Nov. 20, was the heaviest day of the week and of November: $669.2 million left the bitcoin funds, per Farside. [CryptoDataAPI](https://cryptodataapi.com/etf-flows/btc/2026-11), which compiles Farside's settled daily totals, shows the same Friday figure, as does Trading Notified. IBIT accounted for $544.7 million of that session, per Farside, matching SoSoValue's Friday IBIT figure of $544.73 million in the Bitcoin.com report. Farside's Friday table also showed $72.4 million out of FBTC, $32.8 million out of GBTC, $12.9 million out of the Grayscale Mini Trust, $7.0 million out of BITB and $1.7 million out of Franklin's EZBC, partly offset by a $2.3 million inflow into MSBT. Those Friday fund figures also appear in CryptoDataAPI's daily table. Farside's historical IBIT column lists Friday's $544.7 million as the fund's largest one-day outflow, one session after Thursday's $541.1 million IBIT outflow and $582.3 million total.

Only Monday, Nov. 16, was a net inflow, at $7.9 million, per Farside and CryptoDataAPI. The next four sessions were outflows, and each was larger than the last: $239.9 million on Tuesday, $306.5 million on Wednesday, $582.3 million on Thursday and $669.2 million on Friday. The November daily totals through Monday, Nov. 23, are shown in the Black Mint chart with this story.

The week was the fourth in a row of net bitcoin ETF outflows. Bitcoin.com, citing SoSoValue, and Trading Notified, summing Farside, both put the four-week total, covering the weeks of Oct. 26-30 through Nov. 16-20, at about $4.34 billion.

November through Friday is $4.137 billion of net outflows over 15 sessions, with only two inflow days, per CryptoDataAPI's settled table. The three complete November weeks on Farside sum to the same $4,137.0 million, and Trading Notified also put November through Friday at about $4.14 billion. June 2026 remains the largest month of outflows in that record, at $4.51 billion, per [CryptoDataAPI's monthly history](https://cryptodataapi.com/etf-flows/btc) and Trading Notified's Farside sum. October's total was a $515.9 million outflow, per CryptoDataAPI and [Coinburn](https://coinburn.com/news/us-bitcoin-funds-october-outflow-despite-ibit-inflows). IBIT accounted for $3.49 billion of November's exits through Friday, CryptoDataAPI's sum of Farside's daily IBIT figures shows, with FBTC at $217.1 million out, GBTC at $219.4 million out and MSBT at $111.0 million in. Monday, Nov. 23, added another $569.7 million of outflows, per Farside and [CryptoDataAPI](https://cryptodataapi.com/etf-flows/btc/2026-11), so November through Monday is $4.707 billion of net outflows over 16 sessions, with only two inflow days. IBIT's November outflow through Monday is $3.995 billion, FBTC's is $203.8 million, and GBTC's and MSBT's are unchanged from Friday.

Since the funds launched on Jan. 11, 2024, cumulative net inflows through Friday were $52.91 billion, per CryptoDataAPI, covering 719 settled trading days. After Monday's $569.7 million outflow, Farside's running total fell to $52,341 million through Monday, Nov. 23, and CryptoDataAPI also shows $52.34 billion across 720 settled trading days. SoSoValue-based tallies are a little lower: Bloomingbit put cumulative net inflows at $52.84 billion as of Friday, and total net assets at $71.35 billion. Bitcoin.com, also citing SoSoValue, published the same $71.35 billion asset figure and said it was down from $86.2 billion a week earlier, with falling bitcoin prices accounting for much of that decline alongside the withdrawals. Small gaps between providers are common. The daily creation and redemption figures are closer.

Spot ether ETFs had $305.8 million of net outflows in the same week, per [Farside](https://farside.co.uk/eth/) and [SatoshiMacro](https://satoshimacro.com/tools/crypto/etf-flows/daily-eth-etf-flows/), which compiles Farside. SoSoValue, in the Bitcoin.com report, put the ether total at $314.17 million. BlackRock's iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) accounted for $230.0 million of the Farside week, a figure SatoshiMacro also lists and that Bitcoin.com rounded to about $230 million. Friday's ether ETF outflow was $97.3 million, per Farside and SatoshiMacro. Bitcoin.com said the week was the eighth in a row of ether ETF outflows. SatoshiMacro's eight-week table is negative in every week from the week beginning Sept. 28 through the week beginning Nov. 16. Combined bitcoin and ether ETF outflows last week were about $2.10 billion in SoSoValue's figures, or $2.096 billion in Farside's. On Monday, Nov. 23, spot ether ETFs had a further $84.9 million of net outflows, per Farside and CryptoDataAPI: $90.5 million out of ETHA, partly offset by a $5.6 million inflow into Fidelity's FETH.

A daily ETF flow total is a net of share creations and redemptions. It does not count how many people bought or sold bitcoin or ether in the open market. Authorized participants create new shares against the bitcoin or ether the fund holds, or redeem shares and take the underlying asset back. A net outflow means more shares were redeemed than created that day. The tables do not name the end investor, and they do not, by themselves, prove a change of long-term view.

The outflows arrived as bitcoin slipped below $60,000 on Friday, alongside last week's drop in technology stocks, Bitcoin.com said. [The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/11/23/crypto-market-today-nov-23-bitcoin-sits-out-wall-street-s-historic-rally-as-usd1-8-billion-etf-exodus-weighs-on-prices/) also tied this week's price pressure to the size of last week's ETF exits. Bitcoin.com and The Motley Fool describe the price backdrop. They do not demonstrate a cause. Researchers at [Oak Research](https://oakresearch.io/en/reports/markets/bitcoin-cot-futures-unwind-expiry-etfs-shed-1bn), writing on Nov. 7 about the CFTC Commitments of Traders report as of Nov. 3, said a drop in hedge-fund futures shorts around the Oct. 30 CME expiry, together with about $1 billion of ETF outflows in that earlier window, was consistent with cash-and-carry trades reaching maturity without being renewed. They also said the data cannot identify the same funds behind the ETF flows, and that outflows in that window can mix unrenewed arbitrage with directional selling after the late-October Binance incident. Those comments predate last week's $1.79 billion and do not identify who redeemed shares in the week through Friday.

Monday's Farside tables are now complete. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs had $569.7 million of net outflows on Monday, Nov. 23, per Farside, the second-largest session of November after Friday's $669.2 million. IBIT accounted for $509.3 million, the Grayscale Mini Trust for $61.1 million and Bitwise's BITB for $12.6 million, partly offset by a $13.3 million inflow into FBTC. All other bitcoin funds were flat. Spot ether ETFs had $84.9 million of net outflows: $90.5 million out of ETHA and a $5.6 million inflow into FETH. [CryptoDataAPI](https://cryptodataapi.com/etf-flows/btc/2026-11), which compiles Farside's settled daily totals, shows the same Monday figures. We did not find a second, independent daily source for Monday, so the Monday fund figures are attributed to Farside.

USD-pegged stablecoin supply, measured at 7 p.m. ET on [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins), rose from $282.50 billion on Friday to $283.22 billion on Monday, a $0.72 billion increase. That Friday level is the $282.5 billion low we [reported Nov. 22](https://blackmint.markets/news/stablecoin-supply-lowest-since-2025). The gain is small next to last week's ETF outflows, and it does not erase the drop earlier in November.

The Justice Department's [move to forfeit about $1.1 billion in USDC](https://blackmint.markets/news/doj-seeks-1-1-billion-usdc-binance-hack) tied to the October Binance incident is a legal claim on tokens already issued, not a redemption figure in the DefiLlama supply change.

**What is still missing**

Monday's flow reports for spot bitcoin and ether ETFs are complete. The reports below have not been updated for this midweek window.

Two of the usual flow reports have not been updated for this midweek window.

The Investment Company Institute's latest [money market fund assets](https://www.ici.org/research/stats/mmf) report, published Nov. 19, covers the week ended Wednesday, Nov. 18, when assets fell $3.58 billion to $7.98 trillion. ICI said that, because of Thanksgiving, data for the week ending Nov. 24 will be released on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Crane Data's month-to-date figure cited in our Nov. 20 deep dive, a $67.7 billion rise through Nov. 18, has not been superseded by a newer public print in the sources we checked.

LSEG Lipper's latest weekly equity-fund figures remain those for the week to Nov. 18, when global equity funds took in a net $59.23 billion, as reported then by [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/global-equity-funds-attract-inflows-for-a-ninth-straight-week-5041603) and [U.S. News](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-20/global-equity-funds-attract-inflows-for-a-ninth-straight-week). No later Lipper weekly print had been published by Monday evening.

**What to watch**

The Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report is due Wednesday, and the Fed meets Dec. 8-9. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/treasury-yields-bonds-fed.html) said CME FedWatch on Monday showed a roughly 98% chance of a quarter-point December hike, up from around 88% on Friday. [Reuters](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Dollar+climbs+as+renewed+AI+euphoria+fuels+Fed+hike+bets/27389508.html) later said traders had fully priced in a 25-basis-point move. U.S. markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving, and Friday's session ends at 1 p.m. ET, CNBC noted.

*In our opinion: Monday's stock rebound showed up in prices, while bitcoin ETF flows kept falling. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost another $569.7 million on Monday, on top of $1.79 billion in the week through Friday, which was the fourth straight week of outflows, with $669 million on Friday itself. ICI and Lipper have not posted midweek numbers. Bitcoin's jump toward $63,700 on the Nvidia news faded by the closing bell, while Nvidia held a 31% gain. Wednesday's PCE report is the next scheduled test for rate-hike bets that have been supporting the dollar.*
