articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $4.71 Billion in November, a Monthly Record
articles.excerpt: Monday's $569.7 million exit pushed November past June's $4.51 billion mark. BlackRock's IBIT accounts for about $4 billion of the month's net outflow.
articles.body_md:
Investors have pulled a net $4.71 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs in November, the largest monthly outflow since the funds opened in January 2024, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/bitcoin-etf-flow-all-data/) data through Monday show.

Monday tipped it over. The funds lost a net $569.7 million that day, and BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) supplied $509.3 million of it, about 89%, as [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-etf-outflows-set-monthly-record-at-4-71-billion) also reported. Fidelity's FBTC took in $13.3 million.

That pushed the month past June 2026, when $4.51 billion left, the previous record in Farside's data.

**Fourteen red days out of sixteen**

Net flows have been negative on 14 of November's 16 trading days so far. IBIT alone accounts for about $3.99 billion of the month's total. The last five sessions, Nov. 17 through Nov. 23, removed about $2.37 billion.

Spot ETFs hold actual bitcoin. When investors cash out shares, large dealers known as authorized participants redeem them with the fund, and the fund hands over or sells the matching bitcoin. A net outflow means the funds, taken together, now hold less of the coin.

Bitcoin traded at $59,449 at 5:53 a.m. ET Tuesday, down 3.2% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin). It slipped below $60,000 early Tuesday as a Monday rally in tech stocks faded, [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2026/11/24/bitcoin-falls-below-usd60-000-as-rally-on-jensen-huang-s-nvidia-return-fades) reported.

Ether funds are moving the same way. U.S. spot ether ETFs lost a net $84.9 million on Monday, [Farside](https://farside.co.uk/ethereum-etf-flow-all-data/) data show.

Over the longer run, flows remain positive. Since launch, U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have taken in a net $52.3 billion, by Farside's count, so November's withdrawals equal about 9% of that total.

*In our opinion: The number that matters is $197 million. That is roughly the net inflow November would need in its last few sessions, shortened by Thanksgiving, to slip back under June's mark. The bigger stake sits with IBIT, which has carried about 85% of this month's exits. A record built mostly by one fund is still a record, and it tells readers which fund's daily numbers to check first.*

articles.title: South Korea Plans 20% Cap on Exchange Owners, Bank-Led Stablecoins
articles.excerpt: Banks would have to own most of any won stablecoin issuer, and exchange stakes above 20% would lose voting rights after a three-year grace period.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's Financial Services Commission (FSC) released a draft digital asset law on Tuesday that would cap a shareholder's stake in a crypto exchange at 20% and let only bank-majority groups issue won stablecoins, [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261124005200320) and [The Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10947682) reported.

The bill still needs National Assembly approval, then presidential decrees to set the details.

**Who owns the exchanges**

The draft limits a major shareholder to 20% of a crypto exchange. Financial institutions and other eligible owners may go to 34% with FSC approval. Shares above the limit would lose voting rights, and existing exchanges would get three years to comply after they are designated under the law, both outlets said.

Some large owners are above that line. Mirae Asset's consulting arm owns 97.15% of Digital X, the exchange formerly called Korbit, The Korea Herald reported. The paper also said the FSC's materials don't explain how the cap would apply to a parent company, a question for Naver Financial's planned purchase of Upbit operator Dunamu. The FSC declined to comment on specific companies.

An FSC official said at a briefing the cap is meant to make exchanges more accountable and neutral, citing more than 10 million exchange accounts in the country, the Herald reported.

**Banks first on won stablecoins**

A stablecoin is a token built to hold a fixed value, here one won, backed by bank deposits and government bonds the issuer holds in reserve. Under the draft, issuers would be consortiums in which banks together own more than half and hold at least 5 billion won ($3.4 million) in capital, according to [MoneyToday](https://www.mt.co.kr/en/stock/2026/11/24/2026112411151579659) and [CoinDesk](https://www.coindesk.com/policy/2026/11/24/south-korea-regulator-backs-bank-controlled-stablecoins-after-months-of-dispute). Reserves would have to cover at least 100% of tokens in circulation. A fintech firm may still be the largest single shareholder.

The Bank of Korea has argued for bank-led issuance, warning that stablecoins can be used to get around foreign exchange and capital controls, Yonhap reported. Foreign issuers would operate by opening a local branch and registering with the FSC, MoneyToday and CoinDesk said.

*In our opinion: The question worth chasing is whether the 20% cap reaches through parent companies, because that decides what happens to deals like Naver-Dunamu. Exchange owners carry most of the near-term risk, with up to three years to sell down. The next marker is National Assembly debate, though the decrees will settle much of the detail.*

articles.title: BlackRock Opens Hong Kong Money Fund to Stablecoin Subscriptions
articles.excerpt: BlackRock's first tokenized fund in Asia-Pacific accepts the HKDAP stablecoin from professional investors. Retail buyers pay cash, from HK$10.
articles.body_md:
BlackRock has launched a tokenized Hong Kong dollar money market fund that professional investors can buy and redeem with a local stablecoin, the [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/business/banking-finance/article/3375575/blackrock-taps-hong-kong-stablecoins-new-money-market-fund) reported Tuesday, citing a company statement. Units start at HK$10, about US$1.28.

The BlackRock HKD Digital Liquidity Fund is the firm's first tokenized fund in Hong Kong and the Asia-Pacific region, according to BlackRock's [September announcement](https://www.blackrock.com/cash/en-hk/press-release-t2) of its approval. The fund's [product page](https://www.blackrock.com/hk/en/products/352131/blackrock-hkd-digital-liquidity-fund) lists a Nov. 16 inception date and a management fee of 0.31%.

**Stablecoin in, fund units out**

Professional investors can pay with digital cash, including HKDAP, one of Hong Kong's two licensed stablecoins, the SCMP said. Retail investors can also buy, but only with ordinary Hong Kong dollars, the paper and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/converge/tradfi-and-fintech/blackrock-opens-hong-kong-fund-to-stablecoin-payments) reported.

HKDAP is issued by Anchorpoint Financial, a venture led by Standard Chartered. Standard Chartered is also the fund's custodian, administrator and trustee and handles the tokenization, BlackRock said.

A money market fund parks cash in short-term government bills and bank deposits. This one is a "constant net asset value" fund, which aims to keep each unit at a steady price while paying out the interest. "Tokenized" means ownership records sit on a blockchain, so a buyer holding a stablecoin can settle on-chain without first moving money through a bank.

BlackRock's own fund page warns that the fund "is not a guaranteed investment" and can impose redemption fees or gates under stress. It also flags added technology risks from tokenized units.

BlackRock already runs tokenized money funds in the U.S. and Europe, its September release said. In Hong Kong, HSBC launched a similar service using a stablecoin called RedCoin, the SCMP reported.

*In our opinion: The detail worth noting is the split: stablecoin settlement for professionals, plain cash for everyone else. That puts Standard Chartered at the center, on both the stablecoin side and the fund side. The fund's net assets aren't posted yet, so the first published asset figure will show how much stablecoin money actually came in.*

articles.title: Coinbase Wins Final Dismissal of TerraUSD Buyer's Lawsuit
articles.excerpt: A federal judge found Coinbase's own UST page said the token wasn't backed by dollars in a bank account, and barred a fifth try at the proposed class action.
articles.body_md:
A federal judge in San Francisco has dismissed a proposed class action against Coinbase over sales of TerraUSD, the stablecoin that collapsed in May 2022, and ruled that the plaintiff can't amend it again, according to a [Nov. 20 order](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCOURTS-cand-3_22-cv-03561/pdf/USCOURTS-cand-3_22-cv-03561-3.pdf). Judgment was entered Monday, closing the case, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-11-23-california-court-terminates-lawsuit-coinbase-terrausd-445448).

The suit, led by buyer Larry Pearl, argued that Coinbase failed to make clear that UST relied on an algorithm tied to a second token, LUNA, rather than on dollar reserves. It was his fourth amended complaint.

**How UST was supposed to hold $1**

Reserve-backed stablecoins hold cash or similar assets behind each token. UST didn't. It kept its price through a swap system: users could burn $1 worth of LUNA to create one UST, or burn UST to get LUNA back, with traders' arbitrage meant to keep the price near $1. When demand dried up in May 2022, that loop broke. Pearl's complaint says UST had dropped to 35 cents by May 9, 2022.

**What the judge found**

U.S. District Judge Maxine M. Chesney wrote that the same Coinbase web page that called UST a stablecoin also said "UST isn't backed by US dollars in a bank account," and linked to a whitepaper describing its tie to LUNA. She also dismissed claims that UST was an unregistered security, finding the complaint didn't plead facts showing a "common enterprise," one part of the Supreme Court's Howey test for investment contracts.

Several claims were thrown out because they went beyond what an earlier order allowed Pearl to amend, the order says. [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/securities-law/coinbase-persuades-judge-to-toss-terra-stablecoin-holders-suit) also reported the ruling. Black Mint found no public comment from Pearl's lawyers or Coinbase on the decision.

*In our opinion: The lesson in this order is about the fine print. The court treated what Coinbase disclosed on its own listing page as enough, which puts more of the burden on buyers to read how a token works before buying it. Whether Pearl appeals to the Ninth Circuit is the next thing to watch.*

articles.title: EU Proposes Crypto Platform Curbs in New Russia Sanctions Package
articles.excerpt: The European Commission's 22nd package targets crypto and payment networks, including in third countries, and extends a transaction ban to about 60 Russian banks.
articles.body_md:
The European Commission on Monday proposed a 22nd package of sanctions on Russia that targets crypto platforms and payment networks and would extend a transaction ban to about 60 Russian banks, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen [said in a statement](https://cyprus.representation.ec.europa.eu/news/statement-president-von-der-leyen-22nd-package-sanctions-against-russia-2026-11-23_en).

The plan isn't law yet. EU sanctions need the unanimous approval of member countries to be adopted, [Reuters reported](https://uk.news.yahoo.com/eu-commission-proposes-22nd-sanctions-151739377.html).

**Third countries in the frame**

"We will focus on Russia but also include third countries that help Russia to evade our sanctions," von der Leyen said, calling it "a major focus of our new package." The Commission has also set up a Crypto Sanctions Task Force to coordinate the work with international partners. All 60 banks would also be cut off from SWIFT, the messaging network banks use to send international payments, she said.

Earlier this year, Kyrgyzstan became the first country hit by the EU's anti-circumvention tool, over sanctions evasion through its banks and crypto companies, according to Reuters.

**How sanctions reach crypto**

Once sanctions are adopted, EU-regulated exchanges, wallet providers and payment firms must stop dealing with the listed platforms and people. Businesses that serve EU customers then have to screen transfers against the list, the same way banks do. The Commission statement didn't name the crypto platforms it wants to add.

The package also covers energy services, more than 70 additional shadow-fleet ships, a visa ban for Russian ex-combatants and limits on Russian teams and athletes at sports events in the EU, von der Leyen said. Russia's government had not publicly responded to the proposal in the sources Black Mint reviewed.

*In our opinion: The stake for crypto firms sits in the "third countries" line. A platform outside both Russia and the EU can still lose access to European customers and partners if it ends up on the list. The next step is the member-state negotiation, and the final legal text will show which platforms are actually named.*

articles.title: DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Tied to Binance Hack
articles.excerpt: Circle has frozen the tokens and agreed to mint replacement USDC for the U.S. if a judge orders forfeiture, the complaint says. Binance put its losses at $6.34 billion.
articles.body_md:
The U.S. Justice Department on Monday filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC that prosecutors say came from the Oct. 29 theft at Binance, the [department said](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/united-states-files-action-recover-more-1-billion-cryptocurrency-assets-stolen-north-korean).

The [complaint](https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc/media/1473936/dl?inline=), filed in federal court in Washington, D.C., lists USDC held at 36 addresses on 18 blockchains. Balances in the filing add up to about $1.17 billion, [The Block reported](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-23-doj-1-17-billion-usdc-binance-hack-circle-replacement-tokens-445398). U.S. investigators attribute the theft to North Korean hackers known as Lazarus Group, or APT38.

**How a frozen stablecoin gets returned**

USDC is a dollar-pegged token issued by Circle, which can block specific addresses so the coins there can't move. That is what happened here. But Circle told prosecutors it can't transfer the original tokens out of the blocked addresses, according to the complaint. Instead, Circle agreed to issue an equal amount of new USDC and send it to the United States once a court enters a forfeiture order.

Civil forfeiture is a case against the property itself, not a person, so no one is charged in this filing. The allegations have not been decided by a court. Prosecutors also asked a judge to keep the funds restrained while the case runs, after a temporary order granted on Nov. 12.

**Part of a $6 billion recovery effort**

The department said U.S. authorities have helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the theft. Binance has put its losses at about $6.34 billion and said it covered affected users' assets with its own funds.

"Following the Binance theft, the FBI and our partners moved quickly to trace and freeze stolen assets," Brett Leatherman, operations director of the FBI's Cyber Branch, said in the department's release.

*In our opinion: This case shows the trade-off built into regulated stablecoins. An issuer that can freeze coins can also help return them, which is why this $1.1 billion could be held in place for the court. The next step is the court's ruling on keeping the funds restrained, and then any forfeiture order that would trigger Circle's replacement tokens.*

articles.title: CFTC Staff Let Exchanges Count Bitcoin, Ether Toward Capital Cushions
articles.excerpt: A staff advisory sets a 20% haircut for bitcoin and ether and 2% for payment stablecoins, but keeps crypto out of the separate three-month cash buffer.
articles.body_md:
Staff at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Monday that U.S. futures exchanges, swap platforms and clearinghouses may count bitcoin, ether and payment stablecoins toward the money they must hold to cover a year of operating costs, according to a [CFTC release](https://www.cftc.gov/PressRoom/PressReleases/9331-26).

Several registered venues and applicants already hold crypto and had asked whether it could count, the advisory says.

**What a haircut does**

Under CFTC rules, these venues must hold financial resources worth at least 12 months of projected operating costs. A haircut cuts the value a firm can claim for an asset, to allow for price swings. The [staff advisory](https://www.cftc.gov/csl/26-31/download) says staff would not object to a minimum 20% haircut for bitcoin and ether and 2% for payment stablecoins, the same levels staff has accepted for futures brokers' own crypto holdings. In practice, $1 million of bitcoin would count as $800,000, while $1 million of a payment stablecoin would count as $980,000.

Other crypto assets that aren't readily marketable would generally take a 100% haircut, so they wouldn't count at all. Firms are also told to consider "wrong-way risk," the chance that crypto prices fall at the same time the business takes operating losses.

**Not for the cash buffer**

The rules also require a slice of those resources, at least three months of costs, to sit in cash or highly liquid securities. Crypto doesn't qualify as either under U.S. accounting rules (GAAP), so it can't fill that slice, the advisory says.

The advisory reflects staff views only. It doesn't create new rules or enforceable rights, isn't a no-action position and doesn't necessarily reflect the views of the commission, the CFTC said. Bitcoin traded near $61,047 at 5:49 p.m. ET, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The number that matters is the gap between 20% and 2%, which tells firms that regulators treat a payment stablecoin as nearly cash and bitcoin as a volatile asset. Crypto can now help cover next year's rent, just not this quarter's bills. Because this is staff guidance rather than a commission rule, the thing to watch is whether the full commission writes it into formal rules.*

articles.title: Fed's Williams Says Inflation Near 3.5% Leaves 'Work to Do'
articles.excerpt: The New York Fed chief expects inflation to slow to just above 2% next year and hit the 2% goal in 2028. The Fed's next decision is Dec. 9.
articles.body_md:
New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that inflation of about 3.5% is "simply too high" and that the central bank has more work to do to bring it back to its 2% goal, in [prepared remarks](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/speeches/2026/wil261123) in the Bronx.

His remarks came about two weeks before the committee's [Dec. 8-9 meeting](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm), and he didn't say what he wants there.

**Three causes, one target**

Williams tied the inflation to higher tariffs, energy and supply-chain shocks linked to conflicts in the Middle East, and strong demand for chips and other goods used in the AI buildout. He said tariff effects "have largely abated." He expects inflation of about 3.5% this year, just above 2% next year and 2% in 2028, with growth near 2.75% and unemployment edging down to about 4%.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2 percent goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," he said. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/john-williams-fed-inflation-rate-hikes.html) said the remarks indicate higher rates are likely over time.

**Why rates reach crypto**

The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% in [October](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm). A higher rate raises the return on cash and Treasury bills. Bitcoin pays no interest, so higher yields raise the cost of holding it instead of those assets. Williams also said policy takes one to two years to have its full effect, so he said the Fed must stay forward-looking.

Bitcoin traded near $61,047 at 5:49 p.m. ET, up 0.5% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The phrase worth chasing is "over time." Williams laid out a slow, steady path back to 2% by 2028, and he kept his December view to himself. That leaves the Dec. 9 decision and the Fed's new projections as the next test for every asset that pays no yield, bitcoin included.*

articles.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Nasdaq Rises 6.4%
articles.excerpt: The board reversed a Nov. 17 statement that it did not intend to bring him back. Bitcoin rose to about $63,700 as the news hit.
articles.body_md:
Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive Monday, effective immediately, the [company said](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director). The Nasdaq Composite was up 6.4% at 12:52 p.m. ET, per [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/), after falling 10% last week. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC) showed the index up 6.3%, at 24,053.11, at 12:51 p.m.

Nvidia shares traded at $163.84 at 12:52 p.m. ET, up $38.31, or 30.5%, from Friday's close of $125.53, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA). [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/) showed $163.83 at the same minute. An [8-K filed Monday](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000090/nvda-20261122.htm) said the board took the action on Sunday, Nov. 22.

**How the board reversed course**

Nvidia [announced on Nov. 12](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-ceo-transition) that Huang had resigned as president, CEO and a director, and that chief financial officer Colette Kress would serve as interim CEO. An [8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000082/nvda-20261111.htm) listed Nov. 11 as the date the board accepted the resignation.

Board chair Harvey C. Jones told investors on the Nov. 17 earnings call that Huang "voluntarily resigned" after disclosure of "personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards and cultural norms," and that "the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/17/nx-s1-6044213/jensen-huang-nvidia-congress) and [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1036160/nvidia-earnings-harvey-c-jones-jensen-huang) reported.

Monday's [release](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director) said the board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after meetings that left it "satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang's candor and ability to lead NVIDIA." It said the board "received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang's reinstatement poses no national security risk."

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Jones said in the release. Huang said he was taking the role "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." Kress will continue as CFO, and Jones will remain board chair.

**What led to the resignation**

News reports in late October and early November described extramarital relationships involving Huang, including one with a woman whom U.S. officials have alleged was working with Chinese intelligence. [The Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/nvidia-jensen-huang-39d4b34ffaa867b4e669893b5fd5028f) and [Reuters](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-street-futures-rebound-rough-075444520.html) have reported those accounts. The reports have not been proven in court. Nvidia's statement refers to "recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."

On Nov. 17, Huang said in a social media statement that he "did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA" and had "made serious mistakes in my personal life," [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/17/nx-s1-6044213/jensen-huang-nvidia-congress) and [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/report/1035465/nvidia-says-it-will-not-reinstate-jensen-huang-as-ceo) reported. He also said he would be honored to return if the board asked him.

The board said an independent-director committee's investigation "will proceed to conclusion," and that Huang has committed to cooperate. It also said it had formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors, is searching for a chief compliance officer, and will continue to cooperate with government investigations and inquiries.

President Donald Trump said in a social media post that the board had made the "correct and proper decision," [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/nvidia-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-ceo-igniting-tech-surge-5045917) and [Politico](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/23/trump-nvidia-jensen-huang-national-security-01180437) reported.

**The market was already attempting a rebound**

The rebound did not start with Monday's announcement. Nasdaq 100 futures were up 3.3% by 3:51 a.m. ET, [Reuters reported](https://za.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-futures-rally-as-ai-rout-pauses-asian-authorities-prop-up-stocks-4591490), after South Korea readied a stock stabilization fund, Taiwan limited some short sales, and China cut a margin requirement, as [Black Mint wrote earlier Monday](https://blackmint.markets/news/nasdaq-futures-rebound-asia-market-support).

Last week the Nasdaq Composite fell 10.02%, or 2,518.54 points, to 22,617.73, the largest one-week percentage drop since the week ending March 20, 2020, [Dow Jones Market Data](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202611208339/nasdaq-composite-falls-1002-this-week-to-2261773-largest-one-week-percentage-decline-since-week-ending-march-20-2020-data-talk) said. On Friday the Nasdaq fell 5.28%, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.93% to 48,147.33, according to [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-stocks-lower-at-close-of-trade-dow-jones-industrial-average-down-193-5042683) and the prior closes carried by Yahoo Finance and CNBC.

Nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, down 14% on the day and 32.7% below its Nov. 6 close of $186.64, the last session before the Nov. 8 weekend reports, per [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/history/) and [Quantellect](https://quantellect.ai/us/stocks/nasdaq/nvda/price-history/2026-11). Monday's 12:52 p.m. price was still about 12% below that Nov. 6 close.

**What happened after the 9 a.m. release**

Nvidia issued its statement at 9 a.m. ET, [Unchained reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-tops-63-000-nvidia-143519261.html). At 9:43 a.m., the Dow was up 1,059.73 points, or 2.20%, at 49,208.04, the S&P 500 was up 278 points, or 4.04%, at 7,188.39, and the Nasdaq Composite was up 1,328.21 points, or 5.87%, at 23,945.94, [Reuters reported](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wall-street-futures-rebound-rough-075444520.html). Nvidia was up more than 28% at that time. Advanced Micro Devices was up 6%, Micron Technology was up 13.7% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was up 12.5%. CoreWeave was up 25%, IREN was up 28% and Nebius was up 24.4%, Reuters said.

By 10:26 a.m., the Nasdaq's gain had extended to 7.6%, or about 1,717 points, at 24,335.01, per CNBC, with Yahoo Finance showing 24,339.57 at 10:32 a.m. Those gains later eased. At 12:52 p.m. ET, [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/) had the Nasdaq up 6.4% at 24,069.96, the S&P 500 up 4.6% at 7,228.27 and the Dow up 2.9% at 49,561.43. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/.IXIC) showed similar levels at 12:51 p.m. to 12:52 p.m.: the Nasdaq up 6.3% at 24,053.11, the S&P 500 up 4.6% at 7,226.39 and the Dow up 2.9% at 49,553.91.

**Bitcoin moved with the news**

Bitcoin's rebound began before the announcement. It bottomed near $55,700 early Saturday, [Unchained](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/bitcoin-tops-63-000-nvidia-143519261.html) said, matching [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data that shows a low of about $55,711 at 1 a.m. ET Saturday. It was already near $61,200 by 8 a.m. ET Monday, Unchained said.

CoinGecko's five-minute data, as reviewed by Unchained, showed bitcoin rising about 4% from roughly $61,100 at 8:55 a.m. ET to roughly $63,700 at 9 a.m., when Nvidia put out the release. CoinGecko's public chart showed a high of about $63,697 at 9 a.m. ET. Bitcoin later gave back that jump and traded near $61,700 at 12:52 p.m. ET, per [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BTC-USD/) and [Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/price/bitcoin).

**The open investigation and the PCE report**

Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter are scheduled to answer questions behind closed doors from the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence Committees and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party on Dec. 1 and on Dec. 2, [NPR reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/17/nx-s1-6044213/jensen-huang-nvidia-congress). [The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/report/1035465/nvidia-says-it-will-not-reinstate-jensen-huang-as-ceo) has reported the same dates.

The board's investigation is still open. October core PCE inflation and revised third-quarter GDP are due Wednesday, a test for the same rate-sensitive stocks and for bitcoin, as [Black Mint noted Monday morning](https://blackmint.markets/news/nasdaq-futures-rebound-asia-market-support).

*In our opinion: the board put Huang back in the job and said an independent investigation will still run to its conclusion. That inquiry, and Huang's closed-door House meetings on Dec. 1 and 2, are the next company-specific events. Wednesday's core PCE report is the next scheduled test for the same stocks that recouped a large part of last week's drop, and for bitcoin, which rose with the 9 a.m. news after already climbing from Saturday's low.*

articles.title: Strategy Moves $1 Billion From Dividend Reserve to Flexible Cash
articles.excerpt: Strategy's board also lifted its preferred-stock buyback cap to $4 billion after the company spent $211.8 million on STRC shares last week, an 8-K shows.
articles.body_md:
Strategy's board on Monday let management move up to $1 billion out of the cash reserve the company keeps for dividends and interest, and into a pool it can spend more freely, according to a [Form 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1050446/000119312526470961/mstr-20261123.htm) filed with the SEC.

The same filing raised the cap on Strategy's preferred-stock buyback program to $4 billion from $3 billion. Both changes free up dollars for more buybacks.

**Two pots of cash, now rebalanced**

Strategy splits its dollars in two. The USD Reserve is meant to cover dividends on its preferred stock and interest on its debt. "USD Cash" can go to buying bitcoin, refilling the reserve or other capital uses, the filing says. After the shift, the reserve held $3.73 billion and USD Cash $1.09 billion as of Nov. 22. A week earlier the balances were $4.75 billion and $151.2 million, [Unchained reported](https://unchainedcrypto.com/strategy-boosts-preferred-buyback-budget-to-4-billion/).

The filing does not give a reason for the reallocation.

**Why the company is buying back preferred stock**

Preferred stock pays a set or variable dividend and ranks ahead of common stock in a wind-down. Strategy's Stretch shares (STRC) pay a variable rate, and the company has said it aims to keep them near $100, according to Unchained. When they trade below that, Strategy has been buying them back.

From Nov. 16 to Nov. 22, it repurchased 2,183,747 STRC shares for $211.8 million (about $97 a share on average). It paid $147 million of that with money from selling 1,925,676 class A common shares (MSTR) and $64.8 million from USD Cash. After the increase, $1.12 billion remains under the buyback program.

**457 more bitcoin**

The common-stock sales raised $176.7 million, and $29.6 million of it bought 457 BTC at an average of $64,898, fees included. Strategy now holds 851,305 BTC bought for $64.23 billion, or $75,446 per coin. At bitcoin's price of about $62,088 at 11:50 a.m. ET Monday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), that stack was worth roughly $52.9 billion, about $11.4 billion below cost by Black Mint's math.

*In our opinion: The number to watch here is the reserve. Strategy cut the pot set aside for dividends and interest by $1 billion in a week when it also spent $64.8 million of flexible cash on STRC buybacks. Preferred holders are the ones who lean on that reserve, so next week's 8-K will show whether the new $1.09 billion goes to buybacks, bitcoin or back into the reserve.*

articles.title: Cross River, LendingUSA Launch Bitcoin-Backed Loans Up to $250,000
articles.excerpt: Borrowers can pledge bitcoin at 30%, 50% or 70% loan-to-value, held by a third-party custodian. It is Cross River Bank's first bitcoin-secured program as lender.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin holders who need dollars but don't want to sell have one more bank-originated option. LendingUSA and Cross River Bank on Monday launched loans of $10,000 to $250,000 secured by bitcoin, the companies [said](https://www.crossriver.com/newsroom/lendingusa-and-cross-river-launch-bitcoin-secured-loans-giving-bitcoin-holders-access-to-funds-without-selling).

It is Cross River's first bitcoin-secured lending program as the loan originator, according to the release and [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/deals/2026-11-23-lendingusa-cross-river-bitcoin-backed-loans-444842). The bank, based in Fort Lee, New Jersey, has worked with LendingUSA for more than 10 years on point-of-sale and personal loans.

"People who invest in Bitcoin for the long term still have financial needs today," LendingUSA CEO Camilo Concha said in the [announcement](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261123782371/en/LendingUSA-and-Cross-River-Launch-Bitcoin-Secured-Loans-Giving-Bitcoin-Holders-Access-to-Funds-Without-Selling).

**How a bitcoin-backed loan works**

The borrower pledges bitcoin as collateral and gets dollars. Loan-to-value, or LTV, is the loan's size as a share of the collateral's value: at 50% LTV, $100,000 of bitcoin backs a $50,000 loan. Borrowers here can pick 30%, 50% or 70%, and a qualified third-party custodian holds the coins for the life of the loan.

There are two repayment setups. With interest-only, the borrower pays interest monthly and owes the principal at the end. With the no-monthly-payment option, interest builds up and everything is due at maturity; that one is offered only at 30% or 50% LTV. Paying early carries no penalty.

**Rates not yet published**

The companies did not publish interest rates. Rates depend on the LTV, the repayment option and AutoPay enrollment, and are disclosed after an application is received, the release says. Approval also depends on credit history and ability to repay.

**What happens if bitcoin falls**

A drop in bitcoin's price may require the borrower to add collateral or repay, and some or all of the pledged bitcoin can be liquidated, according to the companies' risk notice. A liquidation may be a taxable event, and if the sale doesn't cover the loan, the borrower still owes the rest. Bitcoin traded near $62,088 at 11:50 a.m. ET Monday, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: Selling bitcoin to cover a big bill has always meant a tax form and a lost position; this product trades both for an interest rate nobody outside the companies has seen yet. That rate is the question worth chasing. The 70% LTV setting leaves the thinnest cushion, so borrowers there carry the most liquidation risk, and we'll be watching whether other banks start originating these loans themselves.*

articles.title: ECB to Accept Tokenized Pilot-Regime Securities as Loan Collateral
articles.excerpt: The ECB said assets on EU DLT Pilot Regime platforms can back its loans to banks, with the change planned for June 2027. Bitcoin and stablecoins are not covered.
articles.body_md:
The European Central Bank will accept tokenized securities issued on platforms licensed under the EU's DLT Pilot Regime as collateral for its loans to banks, with the change planned to take effect in June 2027, the [ECB said Monday](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr261123~76b6f57b74.en.html).

Banks holding these on-chain securities could then pledge them to borrow euros from the central bank, as they pledge government bonds today.

**How central bank collateral works**

When a euro-area bank borrows from the Eurosystem, the ECB plus national central banks, it must post approved assets as security. DLT, short for distributed ledger technology, is a shared database such as a blockchain. The DLT Pilot Regime is an EU law that, since March 2023, has let licensed platforms record and settle tokenized securities without a full central securities depository (CSD) licence, ECB board member Piero Cipollone said in an [Oct. 21 speech](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2026/html/ecb.sp261021_1~d190f2c349.en.pdf). A CSD is the firm that keeps the official record of who owns a security.

**The fine print arrives in spring**

The assets must pass every standard eligibility test and reach the Eurosystem through a CSD that settles on TARGET2-Securities, its securities settlement platform. Pilot platforms face extra rules on settlement finality, the point a transfer can't be reversed, and on outsourcing critical functions. The ECB expects to publish those requirements in spring 2027.

"We support innovation without lowering our standards," Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said in the release, which the [Banque de France](https://www.banque-france.fr/en/press-release/ecb-expands-acceptance-dlt-based-assets-eligible-eurosystem-collateral) also published.

**What came before**

On [Jan. 27](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/pr/date/2026/html/ecb.pr260127_1~a946167ce1.en.html), the ECB said DLT-based assets issued inside existing CSDs could serve as collateral from March 30, 2026. On Sept. 21, it launched [Pontes](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/target/pontes/html/index.en.html), which links DLT platforms to its payment system so tokenized trades can settle in central bank money.

The decision covers marketable securities such as bonds, not bitcoin, stablecoins or other cryptocurrencies, as [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/ecb-accepts-dlt-assets-eurosystem-collateral/) also noted. The ECB is still studying assets issued and settled entirely on DLT networks. It gave no timeline for that step.

*In our opinion: the bigger story is where the ECB drew the line. Tokenized versions of regulated securities get a seat at the central bank's lending window, while open-market crypto stays outside. Banks and pilot platforms gain a new funding use for on-chain securities, but only after the spring 2027 rulebook lands and the June 2027 start date holds. Until then, the door is approved but not yet hung.*

articles.title: Nasdaq Futures Rise 3.3% as Asian Authorities Act to Steady Stocks
articles.excerpt: South Korea readied its stock stabilization fund and Taiwan curbed short sales after last week's 10% Nasdaq drop. Bitcoin rose 1% to near $61,340.
articles.body_md:
Nasdaq 100 futures rose 3.3% by 3:51 a.m. ET Monday, [Reuters reported](https://za.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-futures-rally-as-ai-rout-pauses-asian-authorities-prop-up-stocks-4591490), after the Nasdaq fell 10% last week, its biggest weekly drop since March 2020. S&P 500 futures added 2.5%.

Bitcoin moved less. It traded near $61,340 at 5:52 a.m. ET, up 1% in 24 hours, per [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin), and the [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/) read 11, its "extreme fear" band.

**Seoul, Taipei and Beijing step in**

- **South Korea:** The [finance ministry said](https://english.mofe.go.kr/pc/selectTbPressCenterDtl.do?boardCd=N0001&seq=6530) after a Sunday emergency meeting that it will prepare its Stock Market Stabilization Fund for prompt use, ease daily share-buyback limits for three months from Nov. 24 and step up checks for illegal short selling.
- **Taiwan:** The Financial Supervisory Commission barred short sales below the prior day's close, except hedging by securities and futures firms, [CNBC reported](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/asia-markets-kospi-taiwan-china-csi300.html).
- **China:** Exchanges in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing will cut the minimum margin ratio for margin-financed stock purchases to 80% from 100% starting Nov. 30, per the same CNBC report.

Short selling is selling borrowed shares to profit from a fall. Margin financing is buying with borrowed money; a lower margin ratio means less of the investor's own cash per trade.

South Korea's KOSPI still fell about 3.3%, while Taiwan's index rose 2.1%, Reuters said. "This was no longer simply a tech selloff," Deutsche Bank strategist Jim Reid wrote, per Reuters.

**Yields rise with rate-hike odds**

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 4 to 5 basis points to about 4.96%, according to [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/treasury-yields-bonds-fed.html) and Reuters. A basis point is 0.01 percentage point. Traders priced about a 96% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate increase in December, up from about 92% Friday, per CME FedWatch data cited by CNBC.

Higher expected rates lift returns on cash and bonds, which compete with assets that pay no yield, such as bitcoin.

New York Fed President John Williams speaks Monday. October core PCE inflation and revised third-quarter GDP are due Wednesday, CNBC said, and Dell's results Tuesday are another test, according to Reuters.

*In our opinion: the number to watch is Wednesday's core PCE. Analysts cited by CNBC expect a 0.3% monthly rise after September's 3.1% annual pace, the highest since May. Seoul has readied its fund but has not said it is using it. Investors carrying borrowed money in both stocks and crypto face the most risk if hike odds keep climbing.*

articles.title: OCBC and StraitsX Test Stablecoin Payments Into Business Accounts
articles.excerpt: NTT DOCOMO ASIA is the first customer. Payments travel as stablecoins and land as ordinary money, the second StraitsX-OCBC project in five days.
articles.body_md:
Singapore lender OCBC and stablecoin issuer StraitsX said on Monday they are piloting cross-border business payments that travel as stablecoins and arrive as ordinary money in clients' OCBC accounts. NTT DOCOMO ASIA is the first customer, the companies said in a [joint announcement](https://www.straitsx.com/blog-post/straitsx-and-ocbc-pilot-cross-border-stablecoin-payments-into-business-bank-accounts) dated Nov. 23 in Singapore.

It is the second project the two firms have announced in five days. On Nov. 19, StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered said they had finished a [proof of concept](https://www.straitsx.com/blog-post/straitsx-ocbc-and-standard-chartered-explore-interoperability-between-tokenised-deposits-networks) moving tokenized bank deposits between the two banks.

### How the payment travels

A stablecoin is a token built to hold a fixed value, such as one U.S. dollar, backed by reserves. In the pilot, a payer abroad sends stablecoins to a "dedicated wallet address" that StraitsX assigns to one business. That address tells StraitsX who the money is for. StraitsX then runs compliance checks, matches the payment to the right invoice and settles it. OCBC handles the "off-ramp," the step that turns the tokens into regular money in the client's bank account. The receiving company never has to hold or manage the tokens itself.

StraitsX, which issues the XSGD and XUSD stablecoins, holds a Major Payment Institution license from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). Both firms take part in BLOOM, a MAS program for testing new forms of digital money, the announcement said.

"Stablecoins can move value efficiently across borders, but businesses still need a straightforward way to receive and manage those payments," StraitsX Chief Executive Tianwei Liu said in the statement. OCBC's Carmen Chan, deputy head of global transaction banking, said insights from the pilot would help the bank deliver value as cross-border payments change.

[Fintech News Singapore](https://fintechnews.sg/142133/blockchain/straitsx-ocbc-stablecoin-b2b-payments-pilot/) also reported the launch. The companies did not give payment volumes or say how many OCBC clients will join. The pilot starts with "selected" business payment flows, and any expansion depends on regulatory, compliance and operational requirements, they said.

*In our opinion: The customer here never touches a token, and that is the design. The bank keeps the client relationship and StraitsX earns its place in the plumbing, so both sides gain if this grows. The number to look for is volume: until OCBC or StraitsX says how much money moved this way, a pilot with one named customer is still a test drive.*

articles.title: Seoul Court Cancels $16.4 Million of Bithumb's Tax Bill
articles.excerpt: The court said coins traded in Korea were not domestic assets under the old law, but kept about 3 billion won in tax on promotional coin giveaways.
articles.body_md:
A Seoul court has canceled about 21.8 billion won ($16.4 million) of a tax bill against Bithumb, ruling that coins traded on a South Korean exchange were not "domestic assets" that the government could tax under the law in force at the time. The exchange had been billed about 37.9 billion won in June 2023 after a tax audit.

Administrative Division 4 of the Seoul Administrative Court ruled partly for Bithumb on Nov. 13 in its suit against the Yeoksam Tax Office, [Yonhap](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20261120167700002) and [The Herald Business](https://biz.heraldcorp.com/article/10945517) reported early Monday, Seoul time.

### Three disputes, two wins

The tax office made three claims:

- Bithumb should have withheld tax on about 3.2 billion won paid to non-resident customers in 2018. The court disagreed. Crypto records sit on blockchains spread worldwide, not on a server in Korea, so trading on a Korean exchange alone did not make coins Korean assets, it said. A 2020 law that would tax non-residents' crypto income has been delayed to January 2027.
- Bithumb understated its coin holdings by about 10.5 billion won by valuing them at an average cost instead of "first-in, first-out." The court sided with Bithumb, saying no clear accounting rule for crypto existed then. Korean regulators issued crypto accounting guidance in December 2023.
- Bithumb should have withheld tax on coins handed out in 146 promotions between 2019 and 2021. The court agreed with the tax office here and kept about 3 billion won in tax and penalties, Yonhap and [Edaily](https://www.edaily.co.kr/News/Read?mediaCodeNo=257&newsId=01561286645648672) reported.

### How withholding works

Withholding means a company collects tax from a payment before the money reaches the person, then hands it to the government, as an employer does with wages.

Bithumb won an earlier, separate tax case against the same office, which Korea's Supreme Court let stand in December 2024, Yonhap reported. The reports did not include comment from the tax office or say whether it will appeal.

*In our opinion: The reasoning carries further than the money. A court has now said a coin is not Korean just because it trades in Seoul, and Korea's crypto income tax still has not started. For now Bithumb no longer owes the 21.8 billion won, and the next thing to watch is whether the tax office appeals, because a higher court's view would reach every Korean exchange.*

articles.title: Stablecoin Supply Falls to $282.5 Billion, Lowest Since September 2025
articles.excerpt: Supply is down $23.2 billion from its Oct. 7 high after seven straight weekly declines. Tether's USDT lost $7.9 billion in 30 days, DefiLlama data show.
articles.body_md:
The total supply of stablecoins fell to $282.51 billion on Saturday, its lowest daily level since September 2025, according to [DefiLlama](https://defillama.com/stablecoins) data. It stood at $282.54 billion on Sunday, down $4.55 billion from a week earlier.

### How supply shrinks

Stablecoins are tokens built to hold a steady value, such as $1, backed by reserves like cash and short-term government debt. When a large holder sends dollars to an issuer such as Tether or Circle, new coins are created. When holders hand coins back for dollars, the issuer burns them and supply falls. The total is a rough measure of how many dollars sit inside crypto in token form.

### Seven Sundays, seven declines

Measured Sunday to Sunday, supply has dropped seven weeks in a row, DefiLlama data show. It is down $23.16 billion, or 7.6%, from an autumn high of $305.70 billion on Oct. 7, and $30.32 billion below the record $312.87 billion set on May 17.

Three coins account for most of the $18.57 billion drop over the past 30 days:

- Tether's USDT: $174.54 billion, down $7.88 billion in 30 days
- Circle's USDC: $68.66 billion, down $3.60 billion
- Sky's USDS: $3.26 billion, down $3.48 billion, including $2.06 billion in the past week

[CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/categories/stablecoins) put USDT's market value at $174.59 billion and USDC's at $68.38 billion on Sunday evening, close to DefiLlama's counts. The two providers track supply in slightly different ways.

### The wider market

Bitcoin traded at $60,921 at 5:53 p.m. ET, up 1.4% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. The [Crypto Fear & Greed Index](https://alternative.me/crypto/fear-and-greed-index/), a sentiment gauge from 0 to 100, read 11, or "Extreme Fear," on Sunday and has stayed between 10 and 12 for eight days.

The data do not show who redeemed or why. Supply also falls when issuers burn coins they hold in reserve, and DefiLlama does not separate those cases.

*In our opinion: Stablecoins are crypto's cash drawer, and the drawer is $23 billion lighter than it was in early October. Every redeemed coin is a dollar that went back to a bank account instead of waiting to buy tokens, and Tether alone accounts for more than $7 billion of the past month's drop. The first sign of a turn would be a week of net creation at Tether or Circle, and we will check that number again next Sunday.*

articles.title: Trump Hosts Dinner Tonight for 185 Top Holders of TRUMP Memecoin
articles.excerpt: The token trades near $0.89, down 98.8% from its January 2025 high. Two Trump-linked companies own 80% of its supply, the coin's official site says.
articles.body_md:
President Donald Trump is scheduled to host the top 185 holders of his TRUMP memecoin at a dinner Sunday night at Trump National Golf Club outside Washington, with the token trading 98.8% below its January 2025 peak.

The event's [official page](https://www.gettrumpmemes.com/gala-dinner) lists Trump as featured speaker, along with boxer Floyd Mayweather, investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson. The top 29 holders get a VIP reception, and the page says, "There will be no private meetings with The President. No gifts will be accepted."

### How seats were handed out

A memecoin is a token built around an internet meme or a famous likeness. Seats went to registered holders ranked by time-weighted holdings, so the score rises with how many tokens a wallet held and for how long. The scoring window ran from Sept. 30 to a final snapshot on Nov. 16, according to the event page and [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/ecosystems/2026-11-22-trump-to-host-second-memecoin-dinner-tonight-with-trump-down-99-from-peak-444828).

It is the third event for top holders. The first dinner was held at the same club in May 2025, and a holder event took place at Mar-a-Lago in April 2026, [Al Jazeera and Reuters](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/22/trump-to-host-private-dinner-for-largest-owners-of-his-meme-coin) and The Block reported.

### Who holds the supply

TRUMP traded at $0.8863 at 5:49 p.m. ET, up 0.2% over 24 hours, against an all-time high of $73.43 set on the evening of Jan. 18, 2025, ET, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/official-trump). That puts the value of tokens now in circulation near $250 million.

The [TRUMP Coin Club site](https://www.gettrumpmemes.com/) says CIC Digital LLC, a Trump Organization affiliate, and Fight Fight Fight LLC together own 80% of the planned 1 billion-token supply, which unlocks over three years. The site says the token is not intended to be "an investment opportunity."

### Criticism and the White House response

Eight Democratic senators raised ethics concerns about the event in an October letter, The Block and Al Jazeera reported. The Democratic National Committee also criticized the dinner. The White House has said the president's attendance at a privately organized event does not make it a government function, according to both outlets.

*In our opinion: The stake is concentrated. Two Trump-linked companies own 80% of TRUMP's planned supply, so no other holder has as much riding on the token's price. Next on the calendar: a new Congress with Democratic majorities takes its seats in January, and the club's Super Bowl package follows on Feb. 12-14, 2027.*

articles.title: Gate Rolls Back ACE Trades After $1 Million Fusionist Bridge Exploit
articles.excerpt: Blockaid said a privileged minter created unbacked ACE on BNB Chain and sold it for USDT. Gate will settle ACE futures Monday night; Fusionist asked users to pause trading.
articles.body_md:
Crypto exchange Gate said it will roll back all ACE/USDT trades made between 12:55 p.m. and 2:15 p.m. ET Sunday after the bridge for Fusionist's ACE token on BNB Chain was exploited. Security firm Blockaid estimated about $1.04 million was taken.

[Blockaid said on X](https://x.com/blockaid_/status/2124580794144322035) at 2:08 p.m. ET that "a privileged token-bridge minter minted unbacked ACE and sold it for USDT," and that the attack was still going. [Fusionist](https://x.com/fusionistio/status/2124586293812461578), a blockchain game, posted 22 minutes later that it was investigating "an apparent ongoing exploit" and asked holders to pause ACE transfers, trades and bridging on BNB Chain.

### How a bridge mint goes wrong

A token bridge moves a coin between blockchains. It should lock tokens on one chain and create, or mint, the same number on the other. An address with minting rights can create tokens with nothing locked behind them. Those tokens can then be sold for USDT, a dollar-pegged stablecoin.

A Black Mint read of the ACE [token contract](https://bscscan.com/token/0xc27a719105a987b4c34116223cae8bd8f4b5def4) on BNB Chain showed a total supply of about 10 quintillion tokens at 5:51 p.m. ET. [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/fusionist) lists ACE's total supply at about 146.3 million.

### Gate rolls back trades and winds down futures

Gate's [announcement](https://www.gate.com/announcements/article/102911) said it detected an abnormal mint of 5 trillion ACE from the bridge and that its security team confirmed the exploit. ACE deposited after 12:55 p.m. ET in connection with the incident will be treated by Gate as "fork coins" if Fusionist rules them invalid.

Gate switched its ACE perpetual futures, contracts with no expiry date, to reduce-only mode, which allows only closing trades, at 4:15 p.m. ET. It will settle all open positions at 11 p.m. ET Monday, Nov. 23.

Fusionist has not said how the minter got its rights, how much was lost in total or whether holders will be repaid. [TechFlow](https://www.techflowpost.com/en-US/newsletter/146243) also reported Blockaid's estimate.

ACE traded at $0.0667 at 5:48 p.m. ET, down 22.6% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko. Its 24-hour low was $0.0571.

*In our opinion: Gate's rollback covers trades on Gate only; anyone who bought ACE elsewhere in the same window has nothing comparable announced so far. The question worth chasing is how one address got permission to mint, and only Fusionist can answer it. Until it does, any request to connect a wallet or "migrate" ACE deserves suspicion unless it comes from Fusionist's own channels.*

articles.title: Bitcoin Miners' Pay Hits Record Low as 9% Difficulty Rise Nears
articles.excerpt: Hashprice, what a unit of mining power earns in a day, fell to $26.16 on Saturday. Bitcoin's next difficulty reset is on track for a 9% increase on Thursday.
articles.body_md:
Bitcoin miners are earning less per machine than at any point in Firsthand's hashprice record, which runs back to 2013, and the network is on track to make their work about 9% harder on Thursday.

Hashprice, the dollar amount that one petahash per second of computing power earns in a day, fell to $26.16 on Saturday, Nov. 21, according to Hashrate Index data cited by [Bitcoin.com News](https://news.bitcoin.com/mining/bitcoin-mining-profits-turn-ugly-despite-hashrates-return-above-1-zh-s/) and [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/cryptocurrency-news/bitcoin-struggles-below-60000-as-mining-profits-plunge-security-risks-grow-5043790). [Firsthand](https://firsthandbitcoin.com/blog/hashprice-record-low-november-2026-a-petahash-earns-3-percent-more-btc-than-in-june), which keeps its own series, put Saturday morning's figure at $27.14, below the previous low of $27.74 on June 6.

### How miner pay works

Miners collect newly issued bitcoin plus transaction fees for each block they add. Hashprice turns that into a daily wage per unit of computing power, so it falls when bitcoin's price drops or when more machines compete for the same reward. Fees made up 0.64% of block rewards over a recent 24-hour period, both Bitcoin.com News and Investing.com reported, which leaves miner income tied almost entirely to the price.

Firsthand said the drop came from price alone. Measured in coins, a petahash earned about 0.000470 BTC a day, 3% more than at the June low.

### Thursday's reset

Every 2,016 blocks, or about two weeks, Bitcoin resets its mining difficulty so blocks keep arriving roughly every 10 minutes. When computing power grows, difficulty rises and each machine wins less bitcoin.

The last reset, on Nov. 14, cut difficulty 9.13%, [mempool.space](https://mempool.space/api/v1/difficulty-adjustment) data show. Network hashrate fell to about 912 exahashes per second that day, according to Bitcoin.com News and Investing.com, and mempool.space now puts it at about 1,035 EH/s. Its estimate on Sunday called for an increase of about 9% at block 977,760, expected around 8:30 p.m. ET on Thanksgiving Day. The figure can shift as blocks arrive.

Bitcoin traded at $61,180 at 11:52 a.m. ET Sunday, up 1.9% over 24 hours, according to [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin).

*In our opinion: The number that matters is Thursday's reset. The Nov. 14 cut gave miners room to breathe, and a 9% increase would take most of it back unless revenue recovers first. With fees under 1% of rewards, the bitcoin price is effectively the whole paycheck, so the hashrate trend into Thursday will show how many machines still pencil out.*

articles.title: South Korea to Release Draft Digital Asset Law Tuesday, Reports Say
articles.excerpt: Reports say the draft could cap big shareholders' exchange stakes, favor bank-led won stablecoins and make custody its own licensed business.
articles.body_md:
South Korea's Financial Services Commission plans to release the main points of its draft Digital Asset Basic Act on Tuesday, Nov. 24, the [Digital Times](https://www.dt.co.kr/article/12096521) reported. [Yonhap](https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20261121042700002) also said the draft is due this week.

The draft would put exchanges, custodians and won-pegged stablecoins under one licensing law. It could also cap ownership of the largest exchanges.

**Ownership caps and bank-led stablecoins**

The Digital Times said the regulator will first take the bill to its Virtual Asset Committee, a statutory advisory body. A [bloomingbit calendar](https://en.bloomingbit.io/feed/news/124970) lists the release for 3 p.m. Korea time (1 a.m. ET Tuesday). Both outlets said officials are expected to meet the heads of the five won-trading exchanges, including Upbit and Bithumb, first.

Measures under discussion, per both reports:

- a cap on how much of an exchange its largest shareholders can own, with a grace period for current operators, or a limit on their voting rights instead
- won stablecoins (tokens pegged to one won) issued mainly by bank-led groups, the model the Bank of Korea has favored
- custody, meaning holding customers' coins, split out as its own licensed business
- liability for customer losses from hacks or system failures, even when the firm was not negligent

**How the rules work today**

Korean crypto firms now answer to two laws. One requires a filing with regulators and anti-money-laundering checks. The other covers customer asset safety and unfair trading.

The new act would define digital assets in law. Capital, staffing and security requirements would vary by business type, and the papers said some types are likely to need full authorization instead of a simple filing.

**Disagreements ahead**

The commission has not published the text, so these points are reported, not final. Both outlets said industry and government agencies still disagree on the ownership cap and on stablecoin issuers. The draft is expected to reach the National Assembly as a lawmaker-sponsored bill and be reviewed with digital asset bills from ruling and opposition members.

*In our opinion: Korea has policed crypto through money-laundering and user-protection rules; this draft would also decide who owns an exchange and who issues a won stablecoin. Founders and large shareholders of the big exchanges carry the most risk if a stake cap survives, though a grace period is reportedly on the table. The number to look for on Tuesday is the cap itself, and whether it limits shares or only votes.*

articles.title: Fluidkey Says Unpatched Logging Tool Let Attacker Take $1.6 Million
articles.excerpt: The privacy wallet's post-mortem says stolen session tokens hit 52 accounts, and 17 bank account numbers and 54 viewing keys were also exposed.
articles.body_md:
Fluidkey said Saturday evening that an attacker took about $1.6 million from 52 user accounts on Nov. 19 by using two known flaws in a logging tool the wallet ran on its own servers.

The [post-mortem](https://docs.fluidkey.com/security/incident-2026-11-19/) says the attacker also pulled personal data tied to 70 accounts, including 17 bank account numbers, plus the viewing keys of 54 new accounts. Fluidkey said users' private keys never left their devices.

**How the transfers went through**

Fluidkey is a privacy wallet that sends each incoming payment to a fresh address. A viewing key shows those addresses, balances and history, but can't move money.

The report says the open-source logging tool, SigNoz, had stored users' session tokens, the codes that tell a server someone is logged in. With them, the attacker created transfer requests on Fluidkey's servers, marked them approved and raised two-factor spending limits. Small payments then set off app notifications. When a user opened and unlocked the app, it signed the waiting transfer as if the user had approved it.

**The fixes were two months old**

Fluidkey ran SigNoz version 0.121.1. SigNoz published advisories on [Sept. 14](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/security/advisories/GHSA-v549-7j2x-qjm5) and [Sept. 17](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/security/advisories/GHSA-w5pf-xwjh-vr5v) for a missing login check and a database-query injection flaw (fixed in versions 0.141.1 and 0.142.1). The report says the attacker read the logs from Nov. 12 to Nov. 19.

**Where the money went**

The transfers ran from 12:28 p.m. to 1:05 p.m. ET on Nov. 19 across six networks, including Ethereum and Base. Fluidkey said most funds were swapped to ETH and about 887 ETH went into a mixing service, which pools coins to hide their trail. It hired tracing firm zeroShadow and reported the case to the FBI and Swiss cyber authorities. [CyberSIXT](https://cybersixt.com/originals/fluidkey-hack-signoz-logs) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/fluidkey-says-unpatched-tool-enabled-1-6-million-hack) also reported the findings.

The wallet returned Nov. 20 with version 1.79.22. Its servers now accept a transfer request only when the user signs it, and tokens are no longer logged. The report doesn't say whether users will be repaid.

*In our opinion: The private keys stayed on users' devices and the money still left, because the app signed what the server put in front of it. Fluidkey's new rule, that the user must sign each transfer request, closes that gap. For the 52 account holders, repayment is the open question. Fluidkey says it will update the report as the investigation develops, and that update is the document to watch.*

articles.title: Bitcoin and Ether ETFs Shed at Least $1.47 Billion Last Week
articles.excerpt: Bitcoin funds lost $1.25 billion, up from $1.07 billion a week earlier, and the total could change: IBIT's Friday flow is still blank in Farside's table.
articles.body_md:
U.S. spot bitcoin and ether exchange-traded funds posted at least $1.47 billion in net outflows in the five trading days through Friday, Nov. 20, [Farside Investors](https://farside.co.uk/btc/) data show.

Bitcoin funds accounted for $1.25 billion of that and [ether funds](https://farside.co.uk/eth/) $221.7 million. The total is a floor: Farside's Friday entries for BlackRock's IBIT and ETHA, plus ether funds ETHB and FETH, were still blank late Saturday.

**How a fund outflow works**

A spot ETF holds the actual coins. When investors sell more shares than they buy, large brokers called authorized participants hand shares back to the fund and take cash or coins out, which shrinks its holdings. Farside's daily figure is the net of those creations and redemptions, in dollars.

**IBIT led the bitcoin exits**

Thursday was the largest day for both groups. Bitcoin funds lost $582.3 million, including $541.1 million from IBIT, while ether funds lost $131.2 million, $124.2 million of it from ETHA.

Monday was the only positive bitcoin day, a $7.9 million net inflow as IBIT took in $76.5 million. Fidelity's FBTC lost $198.9 million over the week, and Grayscale's GBTC and its Bitcoin Mini Trust lost $148.2 million combined. Morgan Stanley's MSBT took in a net $53.3 million.

**Bigger than the week before**

Bitcoin fund outflows were up from $1.07 billion in the Nov. 9-13 week, when all five sessions were negative. Ether fund outflows fell from $398.9 million. [Block Stream Media](https://blockstreammedia.com/2026/11/22/bitcoin-and-ether-etfs-shed-1-47b-in-weekly-outflows/) tallied the same $1.47 billion from Farside's tables.

Bitcoin traded at $59,225 at 11:52 p.m. ET Saturday, up 5.0% in 24 hours, and ether at $1,660.50, up 6.2%, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) data show. Farside's table still shows bitcoin funds with $53.46 billion in net inflows since they launched in January 2024.

*In our opinion: Monday was the good day, and it covered less than 1% of what left by Friday. The cell to watch is IBIT's blank Friday entry, since BlackRock's fund drove most of the week's bitcoin exits. Two weeks of bitcoin outflows now add up to about $2.3 billion, still a small slice of the $53.46 billion that has come in since launch. Thanksgiving closes U.S. markets Thursday, so next week brings fewer sessions to change the trend.*

articles.title: Chainflip Says Attacker Also Took 122.86 Bitcoin, Offers 10% Bounty
articles.excerpt: The swap protocol's own tally puts the loss near $12.3 million, up from $4.86 million first traced on Ethereum. Its return deadline is 1:38 p.m. ET Monday.
articles.body_md:
Chainflip said Saturday the attacker who drained its vaults also took 122.86 bitcoin, lifting the loss to about $12.3 million at 5:51 p.m. ET prices. The project offered a 10% bounty for the rest.

That is more than double the roughly $4.86 million first traced from its Ethereum vault early Saturday. In a [message to the attacker](https://chainflip.io/return) on its website, Chainflip Labs listed 122.86 BTC, 520.22 ETH, 3,249,631 USDC and 758,141 USDT. [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/chainflip-offers-10-bounty-for-return-of-stolen-funds) also reported the bitcoin figure.

Black Mint valued the haul using [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/bitcoin) prices at 5:51 p.m. ET, with bitcoin at $60,060 and ether at $1,679. The bitcoin alone comes to about $7.4 million.

**Keep 10%, return 90%**

Chainflip said in an [X post](https://x.com/Chainflip/status/2124221824116703335) at 2:22 p.m. ET that it had sent the offer as an [onchain message](https://mempool.space/tx/0f75dbd50f247d4d29ffb5d19dae9907f0322f9ef504720b7e27d2453624f004) to the address holding the bitcoin. The terms ask for 110.58 BTC and 2,618.1 ETH by 1:38 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 23. If both arrive, Chainflip says it will treat the case as a white-hat recovery and withdraw its complaints to law enforcement.

**What Chainflip says it found**

The company said it traced how the attack was set up: funding through the Tornado Cash mixer on Nov. 11, a purchase of FLIP tokens and a validator account registered on Nov. 20. It said it has identified how the signing credentials were exposed and has blocked that route. Those are Chainflip's statements. It has not published a full post-mortem, and no one has been named or charged.

**How the vaults are guarded**

Chainflip's validators must bond FLIP as collateral to join the network, according to its [documentation](https://docs.chainflip.io/protocol/protocol-overview). The vaults move funds only with an aggregate key controlled by 100 of 150 validators through a threshold signature scheme, a method that splits signing power so no single party holds it whole.

FLIP traded at $0.308 at 5:51 p.m. ET, down 35.9% in 24 hours, with a market value of about $26.5 million, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/chainflip) data show.

*In our opinion: The new tally puts the loss at nearly half of FLIP's entire $26.5 million market value. Chainflip's posts and return page don't say who will cover the shortfall: users, liquidity providers or the company. Monday's 1:38 p.m. ET deadline is the first date to watch, and the post-mortem explaining the breach is the second.*

articles.title: Kalshi Faces Monday Hearing on NY Order After Judge Denies CFTC Bid
articles.excerpt: A state judge hears New York's restraining-order request at 11:30 a.m. ET. Kalshi says the wording could close its exchange everywhere; the state says it won't.
articles.body_md:
A federal judge on Friday denied the CFTC's second emergency request to stop New York's case against Kalshi. That leaves a state judge to hear New York's restraining-order bid at 11:30 a.m. ET Monday.

U.S. District Judge Lorna Schofield ruled after a telephone hearing Friday evening, [The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/regulation/2026-11-21-kalshi-faces-monday-hearing-on-new-york-order-it-says-would-shut-down-its-exchange-nationwide-444813) and [Gambling Insider](https://www.gamblinginsider.com/news/204997/cftc-emergency-tro-denied-new-york-kalshi) reported. Gambling Insider said she found the agency had not shown a strong chance of winning its argument that federal commodities law overrides state gambling rules; The Block cited a letter from James' office describing the same finding.

**Why the scope matters**

Kalshi is headquartered in New York. The state's proposed order would bar it from operating within or from New York, both outlets reported. The Block said it also covers contracts offered to New Yorkers.

Kalshi's lawyers told the state court that because of that wording, the order would probably force all open positions to be closed, [ABC News](https://abcnews.com/US/kalshi-prediction-market-crippled-judge-grants-restraining-order/story?id=138329957) reported. A CFTC lawyer told Schofield the order would shut Kalshi down nationwide. New York's attorney general's office replied that it is not seeking a nationwide shutdown: Kalshi could still offer lawful futures and swaps, it said.

**The state's case**

Attorney General Letitia James sued Kalshi in July. She alleges it breaks state laws that bar betting on games involving New York college teams and sports betting by anyone under 21, ABC reported. Kalshi says its contracts are derivatives under the CFTC's exclusive oversight, so state gambling laws don't apply.

**How the fight works**

A temporary restraining order is a short court order that freezes conduct until a fuller hearing. Kalshi is a designated contract market, an exchange registered with the CFTC. The dispute turns on preemption, the question of whether a federal law, here the Commodity Exchange Act, overrides state rules.

Federal appeals courts have split on that question. Three have ruled against Kalshi and one in its favor, according to Gambling Insider and The Block. Justice Melissa Crane of the New York County Supreme Court will hear Monday's request.

*In our opinion: Monday's hearing turns on two small words, "from New York," and a lot of open positions ride on them. If the order reaches past state lines, customers in every state carry the risk; if it covers only New Yorkers, the state gets its rules and Kalshi keeps running elsewhere. Watch the scope Justice Crane writes, then whether either side files an appeal.*

articles.title: Upbit, Bithumb Halt CYBER Transfers After Unexpected Token Minting
articles.excerpt: Cyber says CYBER was minted on Solana and then moved out of its bridge's Ethereum lockbox. The token traded 7.9% lower over 24 hours at 5:51 p.m. ET.
articles.body_md:
South Korean exchanges Upbit and Bithumb suspended CYBER deposits and withdrawals shortly after noon ET Saturday. The token sat at $0.216 at 5:51 p.m. ET, 7.9% below its level a day earlier, [CoinGecko](https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/cyberconnect) data show.

The halts followed what the Cyber project called "unexpected minting" of CYBER on Solana, "followed by a transfer of CYBER out of the bridge's Ethereum lockbox," it said in an [X post](https://x.com/BuildOnCyber/status/2124207519581327394) at 1:25 p.m. ET. Cyber said its team is checking which assets and bridge routes are affected and asked users to hold off for now.

[The Block](https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-11-21-cyber-investigating-suspected-1-million-bridge-exploit-as-upbit-bithumb-freeze-transfers-444810) and [The Defiant](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/cyber-warns-against-bridge-use-after-unexpected-minting) reported that Cyber urged users to stay off its bridge and avoid depositing CYBER to exchanges. The Block reported that the post also told users they don't need to migrate tokens, connect wallets or sign anything.

**What the exchanges did**

Bithumb's [notice](https://feed.bithumb.com/notice/1655756) set its halt for 2:18 a.m. Sunday Korea time, or 12:18 p.m. ET, citing a suspected security problem. Trading stays open, and the exchange warned of sharp price swings during the freeze. Upbit stopped CYBER transfers on the Ethereum network at 2:08 a.m. Korea time, [EconomyBloc](https://economybloc.com/article/126356/) reported from its notice. Neither exchange gave a restart date.

**How a bridge lockbox works**

Many tokens that live on more than one blockchain use a lock-and-mint bridge. Tokens are locked in a contract on one chain, here Ethereum, while matching tokens are created on another, such as Solana. The design depends on the two sides staying equal. Tokens minted without a matching lock can be sent back across to release real ones.

Cyber has not said what caused the minting or how many tokens were affected. The project, formerly CyberConnect, runs an Ethereum layer-2 network for social apps, according to its [website](https://cyber.co). CYBER's market value was about $13.2 million at 5:51 p.m. ET.

*In our opinion: The open question is whether every CYBER token in circulation is still backed one for one across chains. Holders who keep tokens on exchanges are waiting on the same answer, since Bithumb says transfers resume only once the network is stable. Cyber's next update should say how many tokens left the lockbox and how the bridge will be secured.*
